Katarasaṅkhārapaccayā kataraviññāṇanti ce? Kāmāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā tāva kusalavipākāni [V 0.0143] pañca cakkhuviññāṇādīni, manoviññāṇe ekā manodhātu, dve manoviññāṇadhātuyo, aṭṭha kāmāvacaramahāvipākānīti soḷasa. Yathāha –

If it is asked, 'Which consciousness is conditioned by which formation?': Conditioned by meritorious volitional formations pertaining to the sense sphere, there are firstly the five wholesome resultant eye-consciousnesses and so on; in mind-consciousness, one mind-element, two mind-consciousness-elements, and the eight great resultants pertaining to the sense sphere—thus sixteen. As it is said:

“Kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Tathā sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, vipākā manodhātu uppannā hoti, manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā, manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti upekkhāsahagatā, manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hoti somanassasahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā, somanassasahagatā [M 0.0144] ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena, somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā, somanassasahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārena, upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā, upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇasampayuttā sasaṅkhārena, upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā, upekkhāsahagatā ñāṇavippayuttā sasaṅkhārenā”ti (dha. sa. 431, 498).

"Due to wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense-sphere having been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness arises. Similarly, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness arise. Resultant mind-element arises. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by gladness. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by equanimity. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by gladness and associated with knowledge. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by gladness, associated with knowledge, and with prompting. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by gladness and dissociated from knowledge. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by gladness, dissociated from knowledge, and with prompting. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by equanimity, associated with knowledge, and with prompting. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge. Resultant mind-consciousness-element arises accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with prompting." (Dhs. 431, 498)

Rūpāvacarapuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā pana pañca rūpāvacaravipākāni. Yathāha –

Conditioned by meritorious volitional formations pertaining to the fine-material sphere, there are five fine-material-sphere resultants. As it is said:

“Tasseva rūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ vivicceva kāmehi…pe… paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti (dha. sa. 499).

"Due to that very wholesome kamma pertaining to the fine-material sphere having been done and accumulated, as a result, secluded from sensual pleasures... he enters and abides in the first jhāna... up to the fifth jhāna." (Dhs. 499)

Evaṃ puññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā ekavīsatividhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti.

Thus, conditioned by meritorious volitional formations, consciousness is of twenty-one kinds.

Apuññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā pana akusalavipākāni pañca cakkhuviññāṇādīni, ekā manodhātu, ekā manoviññāṇadhātūti evaṃ sattavidhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hoti. Yathāha –

Conditioned by demeritorious volitional formations, there are the five unwholesome resultant eye-consciousnesses and so on, one mind-element, and one mind-consciousness-element; thus consciousness is of seven kinds. As it is said:

“Akusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti. Tathā sotaghānajivhākāyaviññāṇaṃ[P 0.0152], vipākā manodhātu, vipākā manoviññāṇadhātu uppannā hotī”ti (dha. sa. 556).

"Due to unwholesome kamma having been done and accumulated, resultant eye-consciousness arises. Similarly, ear-, nose-, tongue-, and body-consciousness, resultant mind-element, and resultant mind-consciousness-element arise." (Dhs. 556)

Āneñjābhisaṅkhārapaccayā [V 0.0144] pana cattāri arūpavipākānīti evaṃ catubbidhaṃ viññāṇaṃ hotīti. Yathāha –

Conditioned by imperturbable volitional formations, there are the four immaterial resultants; thus consciousness is of four kinds. As it is said:

“Tasseva arūpāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā ākāsānañcāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ…pe… viññāṇañcāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ…pe… ākiñcaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ…pe… nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññāsahagataṃ sukhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharatī”ti (dha. sa. 501).

"Due to that very wholesome kamma pertaining to the immaterial sphere having been done and accumulated, as a result, by completely transcending perceptions of form... accompanied by the perception of the base of the infinity of space... accompanied by the perception of the base of the infinity of consciousness... accompanied by the perception of the base of nothingness... accompanied by the perception of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception... with the abandoning of pleasure... he enters and abides in the fourth jhāna." (Dhs. 501)

Evaṃ yaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ hoti, taṃ ñatvā idānissa evaṃ pavatti veditabbā – sabbameva hi idaṃ pavattipaṭisandhivasena dvidhā pavattati. Tattha [M 0.0145] dve pañcaviññāṇāni, dve manodhātuyo, somanassasahagatāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātūti imāni terasa pañcavokārabhave pavattiyaṃyeva pavattanti. Sesāni ekūnavīsati tīsu bhavesu yathānurūpaṃ pavattiyampi paṭisandhiyampi pavattanti.

Thus, having known that consciousness is conditioned by formations, its occurrence should now be understood as follows: all of this occurs in two ways, by way of the life-process and by way of rebirth-linking. Herein, the two sets of fivefold consciousness, the two mind-elements, and the rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy—these thirteen occur only in the life-process in the five-constituent existence. The remaining nineteen occur in the three planes of existence, both in the life-process and at rebirth-linking, as is appropriate.

Kathaṃ? Kusalavipākāni tāva cakkhuviññāṇādīni pañca kusalavipākena vā akusalavipākena vā nibbattassa yathākkamaṃ paripākamupagatindriyassa cakkhādīnaṃ āpāthagataṃ iṭṭhaṃ vā iṭṭhamajjhattaṃ vā rūpādiārammaṇaṃ ārabbha cakkhādipasādaṃ nissāya dassanasavanaghāyanasāyanaphusanakiccaṃ sādhayamānāni pavattanti. Tathā akusalavipākāni pañca. Kevalañhi tesaṃ aniṭṭhaṃ aniṭṭhamajjhattaṃ vā rūpādiārammaṇaṃ hoti, ayameva viseso. Dasāpi cetāni niyatadvārārammaṇavatthuṭṭhānāni niyatakiccāneva ca bhavanti.

How? Firstly, the five wholesome resultant eye-consciousnesses and so on occur, accomplishing the functions of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, and touching. They do so by relying on the sensitivity of the eye and so on, and by taking as object a desirable or neutrally desirable visible form, etc., which has come into the range of the eye, etc., of one produced by wholesome or unwholesome resultant kamma, whose faculties have reached maturity in due order. Similarly, the five unwholesome resultants. For them, however, the object of visible form, etc., is only undesirable or neutrally undesirable; this is the only difference. And these ten have fixed doors, objects, bases, and fixed functions.

Tato kusalavipākānaṃ cakkhuviññāṇādīnaṃ anantaraṃ kusalavipākamanodhātu tesaññeva ārammaṇamārabbha hadayavatthuṃ nissāya sampaṭicchanakiccaṃ sādhayamānā pavattati. Tathā akusalavipākānaṃ anantaraṃ akusalavipākā[P 0.0153]. Idañca pana dvayaṃ aniyatadvārārammaṇaṃ niyatavatthuṭṭhānaṃ niyatakiccañca hoti.

Thereupon, immediately following the wholesome resultant eye-consciousness, etc., the wholesome resultant mind-element arises, taking that same object, relying on the heart-base, and accomplishing the function of receiving. Similarly, immediately following the unwholesome resultants, the unwholesome resultant mind-element arises. These two, furthermore, have unfixed doors and objects, a fixed base, and a fixed function.

Somanassasahagatā pana ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātu kusalavipākamanodhātuyā anantaraṃ tassā eva [V 0.0145] ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha hadayavatthuṃ nissāya santīraṇakiccaṃ sādhayamānā ca chasu dvāresu balavārammaṇe kāmāvacarasattānaṃ yebhuyyena lobhasampayuttajavanāvasāne bhavaṅgavīthiṃ pacchinditvā javanena gahitārammaṇe tadārammaṇavasena ca sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā pavattati. Cittappavattigaṇanāyaṃ pana sabbadvāresu tadārammaṇe dve eva cittavārā āgatā. Idaṃ pana cittaṃ tadārammaṇanti ca piṭṭhibhavaṅganti cāti dve nāmāni labhati, aniyatadvārārammaṇaṃ niyatavatthukaṃ aniyataṭṭhānakiccañca hotīti. Evaṃ tāva terasa pañcavokārabhave pavattiyaṃyeva pavattantīti veditabbāni. Sesesu ekūnavīsatiyā cittesu na kiñci attano anurūpāya paṭisandhiyā na pavattati.

Furthermore, the rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy arises immediately following the wholesome resultant mind-element, taking that same object, relying on the heart-base, and accomplishing the function of investigating. And in the six doors, when the object is strong, for beings of the sense sphere, mostly at the end of impulsion associated with greed, after the flow of the life-continuum has been cut off and the object apprehended by the impulsion, it arises as registration once or twice. In the counting of thought-processes, furthermore, in all doors, only two thought-moments of registration occur. This consciousness, furthermore, obtains two names: 'registration' and 'subsequent life-continuum.' It has unfixed doors and objects, a fixed base, and unfixed location and function. Thus, these thirteen should be understood as arising only in the course of existence in the five-aggregate realm. Among the remaining nineteen consciousnesses, there is none that does not arise with a rebirth-linking appropriate to itself.

Pavattiyaṃ pana kusalākusalavipākā tāva dve ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo pañcadvāre kusalākusalavipākamanodhātūnaṃ anantaraṃ santīraṇakiccaṃ[M 0.0146], chasu dvāresu pubbe vuttanayeneva tadārammaṇakiccaṃ, attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti cattāri kiccāni sādhayamānā niyatavatthukā aniyatadvārārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccā hutvā pavattanti.

In the course of existence, however, the two rootless mind-consciousness elements that are wholesome and unwholesome resultants first accomplish the function of investigating in the five sense-doors immediately after the wholesome and unwholesome resultant mind-elements. In the six doors, as previously described, they accomplish the function of registration. From one's own rebirth-linking onward, when there is no thought-arising that interrupts the life-continuum, they accomplish the function of life-continuum. At the end, they accomplish the function of death. Thus, having fixed bases, but being unfixed as to door, object, location, and function, they arise accomplishing these four functions.

Aṭṭha kāmāvacarasahetukacittāni pavattiyaṃ vuttanayeneva chasu dvāresu tadārammaṇakiccaṃ, attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti tīṇi kiccāni sādhayamānāni niyatavatthukāni aniyatadvārārammaṇaṭṭhānakiccāni hutvā pavattanti.

The eight sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by roots, in the course of existence, accomplish three functions: the function of registration in the six doors as previously described; the function of life-continuum from one's own rebirth-linking onward, when there is no thought-arising that interrupts the life-continuum; and the function of death at the end. Thus, having fixed bases, but being unfixed as to door, object, location, and function, they arise.

Pañca rūpāvacarāni cattāri ca arūpāvacarāni attanā dinnapaṭisandhito uddhaṃ asati bhavaṅgupacchedake cittuppāde bhavaṅgakiccaṃ, ante cutikiccañcāti kiccadvayaṃ sādhayamānāni pavattanti. Tesu rūpāvacarāni niyatavatthārammaṇāni aniyataṭṭhānakiccāni, itarāni avatthukāni niyatārammaṇāni aniyataṭṭhānakiccāni [P 0.0154] hutvā pavattantīti. Evaṃ tāva bāttiṃsavidhampi viññāṇaṃ pavattiyaṃ saṅkhārapaccayā pavattati. Tatrassa te te saṅkhārā kammapaccayena ca upanissayapaccayena ca paccayā honti.

The five fine-material sphere consciousnesses and the four immaterial sphere consciousnesses, from one's own rebirth-linking onward, when there is no thought-arising that interrupts the life-continuum, arise accomplishing two functions: the life-continuum function and, at the end, the death function. Among these, the fine-material sphere consciousnesses arise having fixed bases and objects, and being unfixed as to location and function, while the others arise without bases, having fixed objects, and being unfixed as to location and function. Thus, all thirty-two kinds of consciousness, in the course of existence, arise in dependence on formations. Therein, those formations are conditions by way of kamma-condition and by way of decisive-support-condition.

Tattha yānetāni ekādasa tadārammaṇacittāni vuttāni, tesu ekampi rūpārūpabhave tadārammaṇaṃ [V 0.0146] hutvā na pavattati. Kasmā? Bījābhāvā. Tattha hi kāmāvacaravipākasaṅkhātaṃ paṭisandhibījaṃ natthi, yaṃ rūpādīsu ārammaṇesu pavattiyaṃ tassa janakaṃ bhaveyya. Cakkhuviññāṇādīnampi rūpabhave abhāvo āpajjatīti ce? Na; indriyappavattiānubhāvato dvāravīthibhede cittaniyamato ca.

Herein, among these eleven registration consciousnesses that have been mentioned, not even one arises as registration in the realms of form and formlessness. Why? Because of the absence of a seed. For in those realms, there is no rebirth-linking seed reckoned as a sense-sphere resultant, which could generate it in the course of existence with forms, etc., as objects. If it is asked, does this mean that eye-consciousness, etc., are also absent in the realm of form? No; because of the power of the functioning of the sense faculties and because of the fixed order of consciousness in the different sense-door processes.

Yathā cetaṃ tadārammaṇaṃ ekantena rūpārūpabhave nappavattati tathā sabbepi akāmāvacare dhamme nānubandhati. Kasmā? Ajanakattā ceva janakassa ca asadisattā. Tañhi yathā nāma gehā nikkhamitvā bahi gantukāmo taruṇadārako attano janakaṃ pitaraṃ vā aññaṃ vā pitusadisaṃ hitakāmaṃ ñātiṃ aṅguliyaṃ gahetvā anubandhati, na aññaṃ rājapurisādiṃ, tathā etampi bhavaṅgārammaṇato bahi nikkhamitukāmaṃ sabhāgatāya attano janakaṃ pitaraṃ vā pitusadisaṃ vā kāmāvacarajavanameva anubandhati, na aññaṃ mahaggataṃ anuttaraṃ vā.

Just as this registration consciousness absolutely does not arise in the realms of form and formlessness, so too it does not follow any non-sense-sphere phenomena. Why? Because it is not a generator and because it is dissimilar to that which is the generator. For just as a young child, wishing to go outside after leaving the house, follows its own father who generated it or another relative similar to the father who wishes its welfare, by taking hold of his finger, but does not follow another such as a royal official; so too this consciousness, wishing to emerge from the life-continuum object, follows only the sense-sphere impulsion of its own class—its generative father or one similar to the father—but does not follow that which is lofty or unsurpassed.

Yathā [M 0.0147] cetaṃ mahaggatalokuttare dhamme nānubandhati, tathā yadā ete kāmāvacaradhammāpi mahaggatārammaṇā hutvā pavattanti tadā tepi nānubandhati. Kasmā? Aparicitadesattā accantaparittārammaṇattā ca. Tañhi yathā pitaraṃ vā pitusadisaṃ vā ñātiṃ anubandhantopi taruṇadārako gharadvāraantaravīthicatukkādimhi pariciteyeva dese anubandhati, na araññaṃ vā yuddhabhūmiṃ vā gacchantaṃ; evaṃ kāmāvacaradhamme anubandhantampi amahaggatādimhi pariciteyeva dese pavattamāne dhamme anubandhati, na mahaggatalokuttaradhamme ārabbha pavattamāneti.

And just as this registration consciousness does not follow lofty or supramundane phenomena, so too when these sense-sphere phenomena arise having lofty objects, it does not follow them either. Why? Because of the unfamiliar domain and because its object is absolutely limited. For just as a young child, even when following its father or a relative similar to the father, follows him only in a familiar place such as the house, the doorway, the street, or the crossroads, but not when he is going to a forest or a battlefield; so too, even when following sense-sphere phenomena, it follows only phenomena occurring in a familiar domain such as the non-lofty, etc., but not when they are occurring in relation to lofty or supramundane phenomena.

Yasmā cassa “sabbo kāmāvacaravipāko kiriyamanodhātu kiriyaahetukamanoviññāṇadhātu somanassasahagatā ime dhammā parittārammaṇā”ti evaṃ accantaparittameva ārammaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmāpetaṃ mahaggatalokuttarārammaṇe [P 0.0155] kāmāvacaradhammepi nānubandhatīti veditabbaṃ.

And because it is said of it, "All sense-sphere resultant consciousness, the functional mind-element, and the functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy—these phenomena have limited objects," thus its object is described as absolutely limited. Therefore, it should be understood that it does not follow even sense-sphere phenomena that have lofty or supramundane objects.

Kiṃ vā imāya yuttikathāya? Aṭṭhakathāyañhi ekanteneva vuttaṃ – ekādasa tadārammaṇacittāni nāmagottaṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na gaṇhanti. Paṇṇattiṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Tilakkhaṇārammaṇikavipassanāya tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Vuṭṭhānagāminiyā balavavipassanāya tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Rūpārūpadhamme ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Micchattaniyatadhammesu tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Sammattaniyatadhammesu [V 0.0147] tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Lokuttaradhamme ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Abhiññāñāṇaṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Paṭisambhidāñāṇaṃ ārabbha javane javite tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati. Kāmāvacare dubbalārammaṇe tadārammaṇaṃ na labbhati, chasu dvāresu balavārammaṇe āpāthagateyeva labbhati, labbhamānañca kāmāvacareyeva labbhati. Rūpārūpabhave tadārammaṇaṃ nāma natthīti.

What is the use of this reasoned argument? For in the Commentary it is definitively stated thus: When impulsion (javana) has occurred with a designation of name and clan (nāmagotta) as its object, the eleven tadārammaṇa consciousnesses do not take that object as tadārammaṇa. When impulsion has occurred with a concept (paññatti) as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. With insight (vipassanā) that has the three characteristics as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. With strong insight leading to emergence (vuṭṭhānagāminī), tadārammaṇa is not obtained. When impulsion has occurred with material and immaterial phenomena as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. With phenomena fixed in wrongness, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. With phenomena fixed in rightness, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. When impulsion has occurred with supramundane phenomena as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. When impulsion has occurred with the knowledge of higher powers (abhiññā) as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. When impulsion has occurred with the knowledge of analytical insight (paṭisambhidā) as its object, tadārammaṇa is not obtained. In the sense-sphere, tadārammaṇa is not obtained with a weak object; it is obtained only when a strong object has come into the range of the six doors, and when obtained, it is obtained only in the sense-sphere. In the form and formless existences, there is no such thing as tadārammaṇa.

Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ “sesesu ekūnavīsatiyā cittesu na kiñci attano anurūpāya paṭisandhiyā na pavattatī”ti, taṃ atisaṃkhittattā dubbijānaṃ. Tenassa vitthāranayadassanatthaṃ vuccati – “kati paṭisandhiyo? Kati paṭisandhicittāni? Kena kattha paṭisandhi hoti? Kiṃ paṭisandhiyā ārammaṇa”nti?

As for what was said, “Among the remaining nineteen consciousnesses, nothing fails to proceed according to its own suitable rebirth-linking,” that is difficult to understand due to its extreme brevity. Therefore, to show its detailed method, it is said: “How many rebirth-linkings are there? How many rebirth-linking consciousnesses are there? By what and where does rebirth-linking occur? What is the object of rebirth-linking?”

Asaññapaṭisandhiyā [M 0.0148] saddhiṃ vīsati paṭisandhiyo. Vuttappakārāneva ekūnavīsati paṭisandhicittāni. Tattha akusalavipākāya ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyā apāyesu paṭisandhi hoti, kusalavipākāya manussaloke jaccandhajātibadhirajātiummattakaeḷamūganapuṃsakādīnaṃ. Aṭṭhahi sahetukamahāvipākehi kāmāvacaradevesu ceva manussesu ca puññavantānaṃ paṭisandhi hoti, pañcahi rūpāvacaravipākehi rūpībrahmaloke, catūhi arūpāvacaravipākehi arūpaloketi. Yena ca yattha paṭisandhi hoti, sā eva tassā anurūpapaṭisandhi nāma.

Together with the rebirth-linking of non-percipient beings, there are twenty rebirth-linkings. The rebirth-linking consciousnesses are the nineteen of the kind already stated. Among them, rebirth-linking in the woeful states occurs by means of the unwholesome-resultant rootless mind-consciousness element; and for those born blind, deaf, insane, idiotic, mute, hermaphroditic, and so forth in the human world, it occurs by means of the wholesome-resultant. For the meritorious, rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere heavens and among humans occurs by means of the eight great-resultant consciousnesses with roots. In the form Brahma world, it occurs by means of the five form-sphere resultant consciousnesses; in the formless world, by means of the four formless-sphere resultant consciousnesses. And by whatever means rebirth-linking occurs in whatever realm, that very one is called its suitable rebirth-linking.

Saṅkhepato paṭisandhiyā tīṇi ārammaṇāni honti – kammaṃ, kammanimittaṃ[P 0.0156], gatinimittanti. Tattha kammaṃ nāma āyūhitā kusalākusalacetanā. Kammanimittaṃ nāma yaṃ vatthuṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā kammaṃ āyūhati. Tattha atīte kappakoṭisatasahassamatthakasmimpi kamme kate tasmiṃ khaṇe kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā āgantvā upaṭṭhāti.

In brief, there are three objects for rebirth-linking: kamma, the sign of kamma, and the sign of destiny. Herein, kamma is the accumulated wholesome or unwholesome volition. The sign of kamma is the thing which, having been made an object, one accumulates kamma. Here, even when kamma was done in the past, even at the head of a hundred thousand crores of aeons, at that moment, either the kamma or the sign of kamma comes and appears.

Tatridaṃ kammanimittassa upaṭṭhāne vatthu – gopakasīvalī kira nāma tālapiṭṭhikavihāre cetiyaṃ kāresi. Tassa maraṇamañce nipannassa cetiyaṃ upaṭṭhāsi. So tadeva nimittaṃ gaṇhitvā kālaṃkatvā devaloke nibbatti. Aññā sammūḷhakālakiriyā nāma hoti. Parammukhaṃ gacchantassa hi pacchato tikhiṇena asinā sīsaṃ chindanti. Nipajjitvā niddāyantassāpi tikhiṇena asinā sīsaṃ chindanti. Udake osīdāpetvā mārenti. Evarūpepi kāle aññataraṃ [V 0.0148] kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā upaṭṭhāti. Aññaṃ lahukamaraṇaṃ nāma atthi. Nikhādanadaṇḍakamatthakasmiñhi nilīnamakkhikaṃ muggarena paharitvā pisanti. Evarūpepi kāle kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā upaṭṭhāti. Evaṃ pisiyamānāya pana makkhikāya paṭhamaṃ kāyadvārāvajjanaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ nāvaṭṭeti, manodvārāvajjanameva āvaṭṭeti. Atha javanaṃ javitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otarati. Dutiyavāre kāyadvārāvajjanaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti. Tato kāyaviññāṇaṃ, sampaṭicchanaṃ, santīraṇaṃ, voṭṭhapananti vīthicittāni pavattanti. Javanaṃ javitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otarati. Tatiyavāre manodvārāvajjanaṃ bhavaṅgaṃ āvaṭṭeti. Atha javanaṃ javitvā bhavaṅgaṃ otarati. Etasmiṃ ṭhāne kālakiriyaṃ karoti. Idaṃ kimatthaṃ ābhataṃ? Arūpadhammānaṃ visayo nāma evaṃ lahukoti dīpanatthaṃ.

Here is a story on the appearance of a kamma sign: It is said that one Gopakasīvalī had a shrine built at the Tālapiṭṭhika Monastery. For him, as he was lying on his deathbed, the shrine appeared. Taking that very sign, he passed away and was reborn in the deva world. There is another kind of death called 'confused death.' For when one is going with their back turned, they cut off their head from behind with a sharp sword. Even for one lying down and sleeping, they cut off their head with a sharp sword. They kill by causing one to sink in water. Even at such a time, some kamma or kamma sign appears. There is another kind of death called 'quick death.' For they crush a fly that has settled on the head of a stake by striking it with a mallet. Even at such a time, some kamma or kamma sign appears. Now, for the fly that is being crushed, at first the body-door adverting does not interrupt the bhavaṅga; only the mind-door adverting interrupts it. Then, after impulsion has run, it sinks into bhavaṅga. The second time, the body-door adverting interrupts the bhavaṅga. Then, body-consciousness, reception, investigation, and determination—these process-consciousnesses—arise. After impulsion has run, it sinks into bhavaṅga. The third time, the mind-door adverting interrupts the bhavaṅga. Then, after impulsion has run, it sinks into bhavaṅga. At this point, death occurs. Why has this been brought up? To illustrate how subtle the sphere of immaterial phenomena is.

Gatinimittaṃ [M 0.0149] nāma nibbattanakaokāse eko vaṇṇo upaṭṭhāti. Tattha niraye upaṭṭhahante lohakumbhisadiso hutvā upaṭṭhāti. Manussaloke upaṭṭhahante mātukucchikambalayānasadisā hutvā upaṭṭhāti. Devaloke upaṭṭhahante kapparukkhavimānasayanādīni upaṭṭhahanti. Evaṃ kammaṃ, kammanimittaṃ, gatinimittanti saṅkhepato paṭisandhiyā tīṇi ārammaṇāni honti.

The sign of destiny is a single appearance that arises in the place of rebirth. There, when arising in hell, it arises having become like a copper cauldron. When arising in the human world, it arises having become like a mother’s womb, a blanket, or a vehicle. When arising in the deva world, celestial trees, palaces, couches, and so on, arise. Thus, in brief, there are three objects for rebirth-linking: kamma, the sign of kamma, and the sign of destiny.

Aparo nayo – paṭisandhiyā tīṇi ārammaṇāni honti? Atītaṃ, paccuppannaṃ[P 0.0157], navattabbañca. Asaññīpaṭisandhi anārammaṇāti. Tattha viññāṇañcāyatananevasaññānāsaññāyatanapaṭisandhīnaṃ atītameva ārammaṇaṃ. Dasannaṃ kāmāvacarānaṃ atītaṃ vā paccuppannaṃ vā. Sesānaṃ navattabbaṃ. Evaṃ tīsu ārammaṇesu pavattamānā pana paṭisandhi yasmā atītārammaṇassa vā navattabbārammaṇassa vā cuticittassa anantarameva hoti. Paccuppannārammaṇaṃ pana cutticittaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā dvīsu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇāya cutiyā anantaraṃ tīsu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā sugatiduggativasena pavattanākāro veditabbo.

Another method: For rebirth-linking, there are three objects: past, present, and not determinable. The rebirth-linking of unconscious beings is without an object. Herein, for the rebirth-linkings of the base of infinite consciousness and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, the object is only the past. For the ten sense-sphere rebirth-linkings, the object is either past or present. For the rest, it is not determinable. Thus, although rebirth-linking occurs with these three objects, it immediately follows a death-consciousness that has either a past object or an object that is not determinable. However, there is no death-consciousness that has a present object. Therefore, the manner in which rebirth-linking, which has any one of the three objects, immediately follows a death-consciousness that has any one of the two objects, and proceeds according to a happy or unhappy destiny, should be understood.

Seyyathidaṃ – kāmāvacarasugatiyaṃ tāva ṭhitassa pāpakammino puggalassa “tānissa tamhi samaye olambantī”tiādivacanato (ma. ni. 3.248) maraṇamañce nipannassa yathūpacitaṃ pāpakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Taṃ ārabbha uppannāya tadārammaṇapariyosānāya suddhāya vā javanavīthiyā anantaraṃ bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cuticittaṃ uppajjati. Tasmiṃ niruddhe tadeva āpāthagataṃ kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā ārabbha anupacchinnakilesabalavināmitaṃ [V 0.0149] duggatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā atītārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

It is as follows: for a person who has done evil deeds and is established in a happy sense-sphere destiny, as he lies on his deathbed, in accordance with the saying, 'for him, they hang down at that time,' either the evil kamma he has accumulated or a kamma sign comes into the range of the mind-door. Immediately after an impulsion process that arose taking that as object and concluded with registration, or after a pure impulsion process, a death-consciousness arises, taking the object of the life-continuum as its object. When that has ceased, taking as its object that very kamma or kamma sign that had come into range, a rebirth-linking consciousness arises, which is bent by the force of unbroken defilements and is included in an unhappy destiny. This is a rebirth-linking with a past object immediately following a death-consciousness with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye vuttappakārakammavasena narakādīsu aggijālavaṇṇādikaṃ duggatinimittaṃ manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Tassa dvikkhattuṃ bhavaṅge uppajjitvā niruddhe taṃ ārammaṇaṃ ārabbha ekaṃ āvajjanaṃ, maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇānīti tīṇi vīthicittāni uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā [M 0.0150] ekaṃ cuticittaṃ. Ettāvatā ekādasa cittakkhaṇā atītā honti. Athāvasesapañcacittakkhaṇāyuke tasmiṃyeva ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

For another person, at the time of death, by the power of kamma of the aforementioned kind, a sign of an unhappy destiny—such as the appearance of a mass of flames in hell and so on—comes into the range of the mind-door. For him, after the life-continuum has arisen and ceased twice, taking that object, one adverting arises; then, because the force is weakened due to the proximity of death, five impulsions and two registrations arise. Thus three kinds of process-cittas arise. Thereafter, one death-consciousness arises, taking the object of the life-continuum as its object. By this much, eleven mind-moments have passed. Then, when that same object has a remaining lifespan of five mind-moments, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises. This is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death-consciousness with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye pañcannaṃ dvārānaṃ aññatarasmiṃ dvāre [P 0.0158] rāgādihetubhūtaṃ hīnārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati. Tassa yathākkamena uppannavoṭṭhabbanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni dve tadārammaṇāni ca uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayamārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ. Ettāvatā dve bhavaṅgāni, āvajjanaṃ, dassanaṃ, sampaṭicchanaṃ, santīraṇaṃ, voṭṭhabbanaṃ, pañca javanāni, dve tadārammaṇāni, ekaṃ cuticittanti pañcadasa cittakkhaṇā atītā honti. Athāvasesaekacittakkhaṇāyuke tasmiṃ yeva ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayampi atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi. Esa tāva atītārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya duggatipaṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

For another person, at the time of death, an inferior object, which is a cause for lust and so on, comes into the range of one of the five sense-doors. For him, after determining has arisen in due course, five impulsions and two registrations arise, their force weakened due to the proximity of death. Thereafter, one death-consciousness arises, taking the object of the life-continuum as its object. By this much, fifteen mind-moments have passed: two life-continuums, adverting, seeing, receiving, investigating, determining, five impulsions, two registrations, and one death-consciousness. Then, when that same object has a remaining lifespan of one mind-moment, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises. This too is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death-consciousness with a past object. Such is the manner of occurrence of a rebirth-linking into an unhappy destiny with a past or present object, immediately following a death from a happy destiny with a past object.

Duggatiyaṃ ṭhitassa pana upacitānavajjakammassa vuttanayeneva taṃ anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchatīti kaṇhapakkhe sukkapakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā sabbaṃ purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya duggaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya sugatipaṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

For one established in an unhappy destiny, however, who has accumulated blameless kamma, in the same way as described, either that blameless kamma or a kamma sign comes into the range of the mind-door. Here, substituting the bright side for the dark side, everything should be understood according to the previous method. This is the manner of occurrence of a rebirth-linking into a happy destiny with a past or present object, immediately following a death from an unhappy destiny with a past object.

Sugatiyaṃ ṭhitassa pana upacitānavajjakammassa “tānissa tamhi samaye olambantī”tiādivacanato maraṇamañce nipannassa yathūpacitaṃ anavajjakammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Tañca kho upacitakāmāvacarānavajjakammasseva. Upacitamahaggatakammassa [V 0.0150] pana kammanimittameva āpāthamāgacchati. Taṃ ārabbha uppannāya tadārammaṇapariyosānāya suddhāya vā javanavīthiyā anantaraṃ bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā cuticittamuppajjati. Tasmiṃ niruddhe tadeva āpāthagataṃ kammaṃ vā kammanimittaṃ vā ārabbha anupacchinnakilesabalavināmitaṃ sugatipariyāpannaṃ paṭisandhicittamuppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā atītārammaṇā navattabbārammaṇā vā paṭisandhi.

For one established in a happy destiny who has accumulated blameless kamma, as he lies on his deathbed, in accordance with the saying, 'for him, they hang down at that time,' either the blameless kamma he has accumulated or a kamma sign comes into the range of the mind-door. And this applies only to accumulated blameless sense-sphere kamma. For one who has accumulated sublime kamma, however, only a kamma sign comes into range. Immediately after an impulsion process that arose taking that as object and concluded with registration, or after a pure impulsion process, a death-consciousness arises, taking the object of the life-continuum as its object. When that has ceased, taking as its object that very kamma or kamma sign that had come into range, a rebirth-linking consciousness arises, which is bent by the force of unbroken defilements and is included in a happy destiny. This is a rebirth-linking with a past object or an object that is not determinable, immediately following a death-consciousness with a past object.

Aparassa [M 0.0151] maraṇasamaye kāmāvacarānavajjakammavasena manussaloke mātukucchivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ vā devaloke uyyānakapparukkhādivaṇṇasaṅkhātaṃ vā sugatinimittaṃ manodvāre [P 0.0159] āpāthamāgacchati. Tassa duggatinimitte dassitānukkameneva cuticittānantaraṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

For another person, at the time of death, by the power of blameless sense-sphere kamma, a sign of a happy destiny comes into the range of the mind-door—designated as the appearance of a mother's womb in the human world, or as the appearance of a garden, a celestial tree, and so on, in a deva world. For him, in the very same sequence as was shown in the case of the sign of an unhappy destiny, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises immediately after the death-consciousness. This is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a death-consciousness with a past object.

Aparassa maraṇasamaye ñātakā ‘ayaṃ, tāta, tavatthāya buddhapūjā karīyati, cittaṃ pasādehī’ti vatvā pupphadāmadhajapaṭākādivasena rūpārammaṇaṃ vā dhammassavanatūriyapūjādivasena saddārammaṇaṃ vā dhūmavāsagandhādivasena gandhārammaṇaṃ vā ‘idaṃ, tāta, sāyassu, tavatthāya dātabbaṃ deyyadhamma’nti vatvā madhuphāṇitādivasena rasārammaṇaṃ vā ‘idaṃ, tāta, phusassu, tavatthāya dātabbaṃ deyyadhamma’nti vatvā cīnapaṭasomārapaṭādivasena phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ vā pañcadvāre upasaṃharanti. Tassa tasmiṃ āpāthagate rūpādiārammaṇe yathākkamena uppannavoṭṭhapanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni dve tadārammaṇāni ca uppajjanti. Tato bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ, tadavasāne tasmiññeva ekacittakkhaṇaṭṭhitike ārammaṇe paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayampi atītārammaṇāya cutiyā anantarā paccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

At the time of another's death, relatives say, 'Dear one, this offering to the Buddha is made for your sake; gladden your mind,' and present a visual object by means of garlands of flowers, banners, and flags; or they present an auditory object by means of hearing the Dhamma and offerings with musical instruments; or an olfactory object by means of incense smoke and perfumes. Or they say, 'Dear one, taste this; it is a gift to be given for your sake,' and present a gustatory object by means of honey and molasses; or they say, 'Dear one, touch this; it is a gift to be given for your sake,' and present a tactile object by means of Chinese silk and fine cloth—thus presenting objects through the five sense doors. When these visual and other objects come into range, at the end of the determining process that has arisen in sequence, due to the proximity of death and the weakening of their force, five javanas and two tadārammaṇas arise. Then, taking the object of the bhavaṅga as its object, one dying consciousness arises. At its end, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises, taking that very object which has the duration of one mind-moment. This too is a rebirth-linking with a present object immediately following a dying consciousness with a past object.

Aparassa pana pathavīkasiṇajjhānādivasena paṭiladdhamahaggatassa sugatiyaṃ ṭhitassa maraṇasamaye kāmāvacarakusalakamma-kammanimitta-gatinimittānaṃ aññataraṃ pathavīkasiṇādikaṃ vā nimittaṃ mahaggatacittaṃ vā manodvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Cakkhusotānaṃ vā aññatarasmiṃ kusaluppattihetubhūtaṃ paṇītamārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati. Tassa yathākkamena uppannavoṭṭhabbanāvasāne maraṇassa āsannabhāvena mandībhūtavegattā pañca javanāni uppajjanti. Mahaggatagatikānaṃ pana tadārammaṇaṃ natthi. Tasmā javanānantaraṃyeva bhavaṅgavisayaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā ekaṃ cuticittaṃ uppajjati[V 0.0151]. Tassāvasāne kāmāvacaramahaggatasugatīnaṃ aññatarasugatipariyāpannaṃ yathūpaṭṭhitesu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ [P 0.0160] uppajjati. Ayaṃ navattabbārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannanavattabbānaṃ aññatarārammaṇā paṭisandhi.

For another, who has attained the sublime by means of the earth-kasiṇa meditation or other such attainments, and who is established in a happy destination, at the time of death, at the mind-door, there appears one of the following: a wholesome kamma of the sense sphere, a kamma-sign, a destination-sign, or a sign such as the earth-kasiṇa, or a sublime consciousness. Or, at either the eye or the ear, a refined object, which is a cause for the arising of wholesome consciousness, appears. At the end of the determining process that has arisen in sequence, due to the proximity of death and the weakening of their force, five javanas arise. However, for those destined for the sublime realms, there is no tadārammaṇa. Therefore, immediately after the javanas, taking the object of the bhavaṅga as its object, one dying consciousness arises. At its end, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises, taking as its object one of the objects that have appeared, which belongs to one of the happy destinations of the sense sphere or the sublime. This is a rebirth-linking with one of the past, present, or inexpressible objects, immediately following a dying consciousness of a happy destination with an inexpressible object.

Etenānusārena āruppacutiyāpi anantarā paṭisandhi veditabbā. Ayaṃ atītanavattabbārammaṇāya sugaticutiyā anantarā atītanavattabbapaccuppannārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā pavattanākāro.

In accordance with this method, rebirth-linking immediately following a dying consciousness of the formless realm should also be understood. This is the manner of occurrence of rebirth-linking with a past, inexpressible, or present object, immediately following a dying consciousness of a happy destination with a past or inexpressible object.

Duggatiyaṃ [M 0.0152] ṭhitassa pana pāpakammino vuttanayeneva taṃ kammaṃ kammanimittaṃ gatinimittaṃ vā manodvāre, pañcadvāre pana akusaluppattihetubhūtaṃ ārammaṇaṃ āpāthamāgacchati. Athassa yathākkamena cuticittāvasāne duggatipariyāpannaṃ tesu ārammaṇesu aññatarārammaṇaṃ paṭisandhicittaṃ uppajjati. Ayaṃ atītārammaṇāya duggaticutiyā anantarā atītapaccuppannārammaṇāya paṭisandhiyā pavattanākāroti. Ettāvatā ekūnavīsatividhassāpi viññāṇassa paṭisandhivasena pavatti dīpitā hoti.

However, for a wrongdoer established in a bad destination, in the manner already stated, that kamma, kamma-sign, or destination-sign appears at the mind-door. At the five sense-doors, an object that is a cause for the arising of unwholesome consciousness comes into range. Then, at the end of his dying consciousness, the rebirth-linking consciousness arises in sequence, taking as its object one of those objects that belong to a bad destination. This is the manner of occurrence of rebirth-linking with a past or present object, immediately following a dying consciousness of a bad destination with a past object. Thus, the occurrence of the nineteen types of consciousness as rebirth-linking has been explained.

Tayidaṃ sabbampi evaṃ –

All this is indeed thus:

Pavattamānaṃ sandhimhi, dvidhā kammena vattati;

Missādīhi ca bhedehi, bhedassa duvidhādiko.

Functioning at rebirth-linking, it operates in two ways due to kamma; and by divisions such as mixed and others, its division is twofold or more.

Idañhi ekūnavīsatividhampi vipākaviññāṇaṃ paṭisandhimhi pavattamānaṃ dvidhā kammena vattati. Yathāsakañhi etassa janakaṃ kammaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammappaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena ca paccayo hoti. Vuttañhetaṃ “kusalākusalaṃ kammaṃ vipākassa upanissayapaccayena paccayo”ti (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423). Evaṃ vattamānassa panassa missādīhi bhedehi duvidhādikopi bhedo veditabbo, seyyathidaṃ – idañhi paṭisandhivasena ekadhā vattamānampi rūpena saha missāmissabhedato duvidhaṃ, kāmarūpārūpabhavabhedato tividhaṃ, aṇḍajajalābujasaṃsedajaopapātikayonivasena catubbidhaṃ, gativasena pañcavidhaṃ, viññāṇaṭṭhitivasena sattavidhaṃ, sattāvāsavasena aṭṭhavidhaṃ hoti. Tattha –

This nineteenfold resultant consciousness, functioning at rebirth-linking, operates in two ways due to kamma. For its own generative kamma serves as a condition in two ways: by the condition of kamma at different moments and by the condition of decisive support. For it has been said: "Wholesome and unwholesome kamma is a condition for its result by way of decisive support condition" (Paṭṭh. 1.1.423). Moreover, while functioning thus, divisions, twofold and more, should be understood by distinctions such as mixed and others. That is to say: this consciousness, though functioning as rebirth-linking in one way, is twofold by the distinction of being mixed with form or unmixed; it is threefold by the distinction of the sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere existences; it is fourfold by way of the modes of birth—egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, and spontaneously arisen; it is fivefold by way of destination; it is sevenfold by way of stations of consciousness; and it is eightfold by way of abodes of beings. Herein—

Missaṃ [V 0.0152] dvidhā bhāvabhedā, sabhāvaṃ tattha ca dvidhā;

Dve vā tayo vā dasakā, omato ādinā saha.

The mixed is twofold by distinction of sex; and that which has sex is twofold there. Two or three decades, from the lowest, with the beginning.

‘Missaṃ [P 0.0161] dvidhā bhāvabhedā’ti yañhetamettha aññatra arūpabhavā rūpamissaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ uppajjati, taṃ rūpabhave itthindriyapurisindriyasaṅkhātena bhāvena vinā uppattito kāmabhave aññatra jātipaṇḍakapaṭisandhiyā bhāvena saha uppattito sabhāvaṃ abhāvanti duvidhaṃ hoti.

‘The mixed is twofold by distinction of sex’: Here, that rebirth-linking consciousness which arises mixed with form, apart from the formless existence, is twofold, as having sex and not having sex, because in the form realm it arises without the sex, which is the faculty of femininity or masculinity, while in the sense-sphere existence, apart from rebirth as a born-eunuch, it arises with sex.

‘Sabhāvaṃ tattha ca dvidhā’ti tatthāpi ca yaṃ sabhāvaṃ taṃ itthipurisabhāvānaṃ aññatarena saha uppattito duvidhameva hoti.

‘And that which has sex is twofold there’: There too, that which has sex is indeed twofold because it arises along with either the state of woman or the state of man.

‘Dve [M 0.0153] vā tayo vā dasakā, omato ādinā sahā’ti yañhetamettha missaṃ amissanti dvaye ādibhūtaṃ rūpamissaṃ paṭisandhiviññāṇaṃ, tena saha vatthukāyadasakavasena dve vā vatthukāyabhāvadasakavasena tayo vā dasakā omato uppajjanti, natthi ito paraṃ rūpaparihānīti. Taṃ panetaṃ evaṃ omakaparimāṇaṃ uppajjamānaṃ aṇḍajajalābujanāmikāsu dvīsu yonīsu jātiuṇṇāya ekena aṃsunā uddhatatelasappimaṇḍappamāṇaṃ kalalanti laddhasaṅkhaṃ hutvā uppajjati. Tattha yonīnaṃ gativasena sambhavabhedo veditabbo. Etāsu hi –

‘Two or three decades, from the lowest, with the beginning’: Herein, that rebirth-linking consciousness mixed with form, which is primary in both the mixed and the unmixed, together with it, two decades arise from the lowest by way of the base-body decade, or three decades by way of the base-body-sex decade. There is no further diminution of form than this. When this arises with such a minimal measure, in the two modes of birth called egg-born and womb-born, it arises, heated by the heat of its generation, having received the designation ‘kalala’—a measure comparable to a drop of oil or clarified butter taken up on the tip of a single thread. Herein, the distinction of origins by way of destinations of birth should be understood. For in these:

Niraye bhummavajjesu, devesu ca na yoniyo;

Tisso purimikā honti, catassopi gatittaye.

In hells, and among the devas excluding the earth-bound, the first three modes of birth do not exist; all four exist in the three destinations.

Tattha devesu cāti casaddena yathā niraye ca bhummavajjesu ca devesu, evaṃ nijjhāmataṇhikapetesu ca purimikā tisso yoniyo na santīti veditabbā. Opapātikā eva hi te honti. Sese pana tiracchānapettivisayamanussasaṅkhāte gatittaye pubbe vajjitabhummadevesu ca catasso yoniyo honti. Tattha –

Herein, by the word ‘and’ in ‘and among devas,’ it should be understood that just as in hells and among the devas excluding the earth-bound, so too among the flame-hungry ghosts, the first three modes of birth do not exist. For they are only spontaneously arisen. However, in the remaining three destinations—namely, the animal realm, the ghost realm, and the human realm—and among the earth-bound devas previously excluded, all four modes of birth exist. Herein—

Tiṃsa nava ceva rūpīsu, sattati ukkaṃsatova rūpāni;

Saṃsedajopapātīsu, atha vā avakaṃsato tiṃsa.

Thirty-nine in those with form, seventy forms at most; in moisture-born and spontaneously arisen, or thirty at least.

Rūpībrahmesu [V 0.0153] tāva opapātikayonikesu cakkhusotavatthudasakānaṃ jīvitanavakassa cāti catunnaṃ kalāpānaṃ vasena tiṃsa ca nava ca paṭisandhiviññāṇena saha rūpāni uppajjanti. Rūpībrahme pana ṭhapetvā aññesu saṃsedajaopapātikesu ukkaṃsato cakkhusotaghānajivhākāyabhāvavatthudasakānaṃ [P 0.0162] vasena sattati. Tāni ca niccaṃ devesu. Tattha vaṇṇo gandho raso ojā catasso cāpi dhātuyo cakkhupasādo jīvitindriyanti ayaṃ dasarūpaparimāṇo rūpapuñjo cakkhudasako nāma. Evaṃ sesā veditabbā. Avakaṃsato pana jaccandhabadhiraaghānakanapuṃsakassa jivhākāyavatthudasakānaṃ vasena tiṃsa rūpāni uppajjanti. Ukkaṃsāvakaṃsānaṃ pana antare anurūpato vikappo veditabbo.

First, among the spontaneously born form-realm Brahmās, thirty-nine material phenomena arise together with the rebirth-linking consciousness, by way of four kalāpas: the eye-decad, the ear-decad, the heart-base decad, and the life-nonad. But excluding the form-realm Brahmās, in other moisture-born and spontaneously born beings, seventy material phenomena at most arise, by way of the eye-decad, ear-decad, nose-decad, tongue-decad, body-decad, sex-decad, and heart-base decad. And these exist constantly among deities. Therein, colour, odour, taste, nutritive essence, the four elements, eye-sensitivity, and the life faculty—this aggregate of ten material phenomena is called the eye-decad. The rest should be understood similarly. But at the minimum, for one born blind, deaf, without a sense of smell, or sexless, thirty material phenomena arise by way of the tongue-decad, body-decad, and heart-base decad. But between the maximum and minimum, the variations should be understood accordingly.

Evaṃ viditvā puna –

Having understood thus, further:

Khandhārammaṇagatihetu-vedanāpītivitakkavicārehi;

Bhedābhedaviseso, cutisandhīnaṃ pariññeyyo.

The distinction of difference and non-difference in death and rebirth-linking should be understood by means of aggregates, objects, destinations, causes, feeling, rapture, initial thought, and sustained thought.

Yāhesā [M 0.0154] missāmissato duvidhā paṭisandhi, yā cassā atītānantarā cuti, tāsaṃ imehi khandhādīhi bhedābhedaviseso ñātabboti attho.

This rebirth, which is twofold as mixed and unmixed, and its immediately preceding death—the distinction of difference and non-difference regarding them should be understood by means of these aggregates and so on. This is the meaning.

Kathaṃ? Kadāci catukkhandhāya āruppacutiyā anantarā catukkhandhāva ārammaṇatopi abhinnā paṭisandhi hoti, kadāci amahaggatabahiddhārammaṇāya mahaggataajjhattārammaṇā. Ayaṃ tāva arūpabhūmīsuyeva nayo. Kadāci pana catukkhandhāya āruppacutiyā anantarā pañcakkhandhā kāmāvacarā paṭisandhi. Kadāci pañcakkhandhāya kāmāvacaracutiyā rūpāvacaracutiyā vā anantarā catukkhandhā āruppapaṭisandhi. Evaṃ atītārammaṇacutiyā atītanavattabbapaccuppannārammaṇā paṭisandhi, ekaccasugaticutiyā ekaccaduggatipaṭisandhi, ahetukacutiyā sahetukapaṭisandhi, duhetukacutiyā tihetukapaṭisandhi, upekkhāsahagatacutiyā somanassasahagatapaṭisandhi, appītikacutiyā sappītikapaṭisandhi, avitakkacutiyā savitakkapaṭisandhi, avicāracutiyā savicārapaṭisandhi, avitakkaavicāracutiyā savitakkasavicārapaṭisandhīti tassa tassa viparītato ca yathāyogaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

How? Sometimes, immediately after passing away from the formless realm with four aggregates, rebirth occurs with four aggregates, even with an object that is not different. Sometimes, from a non-sublime, external object, rebirth occurs with a sublime, internal object. This, for a start, is the way in the formless realms. Sometimes, immediately after passing away from the formless realm with four aggregates, rebirth occurs in the sense-sphere with five aggregates. Sometimes, immediately after passing away from the sense-sphere or the form-sphere with five aggregates, rebirth occurs in the formless realm with four aggregates. Thus, from a death with a past object, rebirth with a past, inexpressible, or present object; from a death in a certain good destination, rebirth in a certain bad destination; from a rootless death, rebirth with roots; from a two-rooted death, rebirth with three roots; from a death accompanied by equanimity, rebirth accompanied by joy; from a death without rapture, rebirth with rapture; from a death without initial thought, rebirth with initial thought; from a death without sustained thought, rebirth with sustained thought; from a death without initial thought and sustained thought, rebirth with initial thought and sustained thought. And for each of these, the opposite should be applied as is appropriate.

Laddhappaccayamitidhamma-mattametaṃ [V 0.0154] bhavantaramupeti;

Nāssa tato saṅkanti, na tato hetuṃ vinā hoti.

This mere phenomenon that has obtained its conditions passes on to another existence. There is no transition of it from that, nor does it occur from that without a cause.

Iti [P 0.0163] hetaṃ laddhapaccayaṃ rūpārūpadhammamattaṃ uppajjamānaṃ bhavantaraṃ upetīti vuccati, na satto, na jīvo. Tassa nāpi atītabhavato idha saṅkanti atthi, nāpi tato hetuṃ vinā idha pātubhāvo. Tayidaṃ pākaṭena manussacutipaṭisandhikkamena pakāsayissāma –

Thus, it is said that this mere material and immaterial phenomenon, having obtained its conditions, arises and proceeds to another becoming—not a being, not a soul. For it, there is neither a transition from a past existence to this, nor a manifestation here from that without a cause. We will explain this clearly through the evident sequence of human death and rebirth-linking.

Atītabhavasmiñhi sarasena upakkamena vā samāsannamaraṇassa asayhānaṃ sabbaṅgapaccaṅgasandhibandhanacchedakānaṃ māraṇantikavedanāsattānaṃ sannipātaṃ asahantassa ātape pakkhittaharitatālapaṇṇamiva kamena upasussamāne sarīre niruddhesu cakkhādīsu indriyesu hadayavatthumatte patiṭṭhitesu kāyindriyamanindriyajīvitindriyesu taṅkhaṇāvasesaṃ hadayavatthusannissitaṃ viññāṇaṃ garusamāsevitāsannapubbakatānaṃ aññataraṃ laddhāvasesapaccayasaṅkhārasaṅkhātaṃ kammaṃ vā tadupaṭṭhāpitaṃ vā kammanimittagatinimittasaṅkhātaṃ visayamārabbha pavattati. Tadevaṃ pavattamānaṃ taṇhāavijjānaṃ appahīnattā avijjāpaṭicchāditādīnave tasmiṃ visaye taṇhā nāmeti[M 0.0155], sahajātasaṅkhārā khipanti. Taṃ santativasena taṇhāya nāmiyamānaṃ saṅkhārehi khippamānaṃ orimatīrarukkhavinibaddharajjumālambitvā mātikātikkamako viya purimañca nissayaṃ jahati, aparañca kammasamuṭṭhāpitaṃ nissayaṃ assādayamānaṃ vā anassādayamānaṃ vā ārammaṇādīhiyeva paccayehi pavattati.

In a past existence, for one approaching death either through its natural course or through some external cause, unable to endure the convergence of unbearable, death-pangs that sever all major and minor limbs, joints, and ligaments—as the body gradually dries up like a green palm leaf cast in the sun, when the faculties of the eye and so on have ceased, and the body faculty, mind faculty, and life faculty remain established only in the heart-base—at that very moment, the consciousness dependent on the heart-base proceeds by taking as its object either kamma (which is a formation that has obtained its remaining conditions, being one of the heavily practiced, near-at-hand, or previously performed actions) or a kamma sign or a destiny sign (which are presented by that kamma). As it thus proceeds, due to the non-abandonment of craving and ignorance, craving inclines it toward that object, whose dangers are concealed by ignorance, and the co-nascent formations propel it. Being inclined by craving and propelled by formations in the continuity of the process, like one crossing a channel by grasping a rope tied to a tree on the near shore, it abandons the former support and, either delighting or not delighting in the new support produced by kamma, proceeds solely by means of conditions such as the object and so on.

Ettha ca purimaṃ cavanato cuti, pacchimaṃ bhavantarādipaṭisandhānato paṭisandhīti vuccati. Tadetaṃ nāpi purimabhavā idha āgataṃ, nāpi tato kammasaṅkhāranativisayādihetuṃ vinā pātubhūtanti veditabbaṃ.

Herein, the former, from passing away, is called 'death'; the latter, from linking to another existence, is called 'rebirth-linking.' It should be understood that this is neither something that has come here from a previous existence, nor has it arisen without a cause from that, such as kamma, formations, inclination, and object.

Siyuṃ nidassanānettha, paṭighosādikā atha;

Santānabandhato natthi, ekatā nāpi nānatā.

Herein there would be examples, such as an echo; from the continuity of the stream, there is neither identity nor difference.

Ettha [P 0.0164] cetassa viññāṇassa purimabhavato idha anāgamane atītabhavapariyāpannahetūhi ca uppāde paṭighosapadīpamuddāpaṭibimbappakārā dhammā nidassanāni siyuṃ. Yathā hi paṭighosapadīpamuddacchāyā [V 0.0155] saddādihetukā aññatra agantvā honti, evameva idaṃ cittaṃ. Ettha ca ‘santānabandhato natthi ekatā nāpi nānatā’. Yadi hi santānabandhe sati ekantamekatā bhaveyya, na khīrato dadhi sambhūtaṃ siyā. Athāpi ekantanānatā bhaveyya, na khīrassādhīno dadhi siyā. Esa nayo sabbahetuhetusamuppannesu. Evañca sati sabbalokavohāralopo siyā. So ca aniṭṭho. Tasmā ettha na ekantamekatā vā nānatā vā upagantabbāti.

Here, for the non-arrival of this consciousness from a previous existence to this present existence, and for its arising by causes included in the past existence, phenomena such as echoes, lamps, seals, and reflections would be examples. Just as echoes, lamps, seals, and shadows, being caused by sound and so on, occur without having come from elsewhere, so too is this mind. Here, 'due to the continuity of the stream, there is neither identity nor difference.' For if there were absolute identity in the continuity of the stream, curd would not arise from milk. And if there were absolute difference, curd would not be dependent on milk. This principle applies to all causally arisen phenomena. If this were so, all worldly conventions would be destroyed—which is undesirable. Therefore, neither absolute identity nor absolute difference should be accepted here.

Etthāha – nanu evaṃ asaṅkantipātubhāve sati ye imasmiṃ manussattabhāve khandhā, tesaṃ niruddhattā phalapaccayassa ca kammassa tattha agamanato aññassa aññato ca taṃ phalaṃ siyā? Upabhuñjake ca asati kassa taṃ phalaṃ siyā? Tasmā na sundaramidaṃ vidhānanti. Tatridaṃ vuccati –

Here one might say: 'If there is such a non-transference and appearance, then since the aggregates in this human existence have ceased and the kamma that is the condition for the fruit has not gone there, would that fruit not belong to another or arise from another? And if there is no experiencer, whose fruit would that be? Therefore, this explanation is unsatisfactory.' To this, it is said:

Santāne yaṃ phalaṃ etaṃ, nāññassa na ca aññato;

Bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro, etassatthassa sādhako.

This fruit, which is in the continuum, is not of another, nor from another. The preparation of seeds demonstrates this meaning.

Ekasantānasmiñhi phalamuppajjamānaṃ tattha ekantaṃ ekattanānattānaṃ paṭisiddhattā aññassāti vā aññatoti vā na hoti. Etassa ca panatthassa bījānaṃ abhisaṅkhāro sādhako. Ambabījādīnañhi abhisaṅkhāresu katesu tassa bījassa santāne laddhapaccayo kālantare phalaviseso uppajjamāno na aññabījānaṃ nāpi aññābhisaṅkhārapaccayā uppajjati, na ca tāni bījāni [M 0.0156] te abhisaṅkhārā vā phalaṭṭhānaṃ pāpuṇanti. Evaṃ sampadamidaṃ veditabbaṃ. Vijjāsipposadhādīhi cāpi bālasarīre upayuttehi kālantare vuḍḍhasarīrādīsu phaladehi ayamattho veditabbo.

For when a fruit arises in a single continuum, due to the rejection of absolute identity and difference therein, it is not of another nor from another. And the preparation of seeds demonstrates this meaning. When mango seeds and others are prepared, a specific fruit that arises in the continuum of that seed at a later time, having obtained its conditions, does not arise from other seeds or from other preparations as its condition, nor do those seeds or preparations reach the state of the fruit. This should be understood accordingly. Similarly, this meaning should be understood in the case of knowledge, skills, medicine, and so on, which, though applied to the body of a child, yield results in the body of an adult at a later time.

Yampi vuttaṃ ‘upabhuñjake ca asati kassa taṃ phalaṃ siyā’ti? Tattha –

As for what was said, 'And if there is no experiencer, whose fruit would that be?'—in that regard:

Phalassuppattiyā eva, siddhā bhuñjakasammuti;

Phaluppādena rukkhassa, yathā phalati sammuti.

The designation 'experiencer' is established just by the arising of a fruit, just as by the production of fruit, a tree is designated as 'fruiting.'

Yathā [P 0.0165] hi rukkhasaṅkhātānaṃ dhammānaṃ ekadesabhūtassa rukkhaphalassa uppattiyā eva rukkho phalatīti [V 0.0156] vā phalitoti vā vuccati, tathā devamanussasaṅkhātānaṃ khandhānaṃ ekadesabhūtassa upabhogasaṅkhātassa sukhadukkhaphalassa uppādeneva devo vā manusso vā upabhuñjatīti vā sukhitoti vā dukkhitoti vā vuccati. Tasmā na ettha aññena upabhuñjakena nāma koci attho atthīti.

Just as by the arising of a fruit, which is a part of the phenomena designated as a 'tree,' the tree is said 'to bear fruit' or 'to be fruiting'; so too, by the arising of the fruit of pleasure and pain, designated as 'experience,' which is a part of the aggregates designated as a 'god' or 'human,' the god or human is said 'to experience,' or 'to be happy' or 'to be unhappy.' Therefore, there is no need here for any other so-called experiencer.

Yopi vadeyya – ‘evaṃ santepi ete saṅkhārā vijjamānā vā phalassa paccayā siyuṃ, avijjamānā vā. Yadi ca vijjamānā pavattikkhaṇeyeva nesaṃ vipākena bhavitabbaṃ. Atha avijjamānā, pavattito pubbe ca pacchā ca niccaṃ phalāvahā siyu’nti. So evaṃ vattabbo –

One who might say, 'Even so, these formations might be conditions for the fruit whether existing or non-existing. If existing, their result should occur at the very moment of their occurrence. But if non-existing, they would constantly produce results both before and after their occurrence,' should be told thus:

Katattā paccayā ete, na ca niccaṃ phalāvahā;

Pāṭibhogādikaṃ tattha, veditabbaṃ nidassanaṃ.

These are conditions by virtue of having been done, and they do not constantly produce fruit; the example of a guarantor and the like should be understood in this regard.

Katattā eva hi saṅkhārā attano phalassa paccayā honti, na vijjamānattā vā avijjamānattā vā. Yathāha “kāmāvacarassa kusalassa kammassa katattā upacitattā vipākaṃ cakkhuviññāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hotī”tiādi (dha. sa. 431). Yathārahassa attano phalassa ca paccayā hutvā na puna phalāvahā honti vipakkavipākattā. Etassa catthassa vibhāvane idaṃ pāṭibhogādikaṃ nidassanaṃ veditabbaṃ.

For formations are the condition for their own result by virtue of having been done, not by virtue of their existence or non-existence. As it is said: 'Due to the performance and accumulation of wholesome kamma pertaining to the sense sphere, resultant eye-consciousness has arisen,' and so on (Dhs. 431). Having become the condition for their own appropriate result, they do not produce further results, because their result has ripened. To clarify this meaning, this example of a guarantor and the like should be understood.

Yathā hi loke yo kassaci atthassa niyyātanatthaṃ pāṭibhogo hoti, bhaṇḍaṃ vā kiṇāti, iṇaṃ vā gaṇhāti. Tassa taṃ kiriyākaraṇamattameva tadatthaniyyātanādimhi paccayo hoti, na kiriyāya vijjamānatā vā avijjamānatā vā. Na ca tadatthaniyyātanādito parampi dhārakova [M 0.0157] hoti. Kasmā? Niyyātanādīnaṃ katattā. Evaṃ katattāva saṅkhārāpi attano phalassa paccayā honti, na ca yathārahaṃ phaladānato parampi phalāvahā hontīti. Ettāvatā missāmissavasena dvidhāpi pavattamānassa paṭisandhiviññāṇassa saṅkhārapaccayā pavatti dīpitā hoti.

Just as in the world, when someone acts as a guarantor for some purpose, or buys goods, or takes a loan, the mere performance of that action is the condition for the accomplishment of that purpose and so on, not the existence or non-existence of the action. Nor does one continue to be a debtor after that purpose has been accomplished. Why? Because of the accomplishment having been done. Similarly, formations are the condition for their own result by virtue of having been done, and they do not continue to produce results beyond the appropriate giving of the fruit. Thus far, the process of rebirth-linking consciousness—which proceeds in two ways, as mixed and unmixed—conditioned by formations has been explained.

Idāni sabbesvetesu battiṃsaviññāṇesu sammohavighātatthaṃ –

Now, to dispel confusion regarding all these thirty-two consciousnesses:

Paṭisandhippavattīnaṃ[V 0.0157], vasenete bhavādisu;

Vijānitabbā saṅkhārā, yathā yesañca paccayā.

By way of rebirth-linking and the course of existence, in states of being and so forth, these formations should be understood, how and for which they are conditions.

Tattha [P 0.0166] tayo bhavā, catasso yoniyo, pañca gatiyo, satta viññāṇaṭṭhitiyo, nava sattāvāsāti ete bhavādayo nāma. Etesu bhavādīsu paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca ete yesaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ paccayā yathā ca paccayā honti tathā vijānitabbāti attho.

Herein, the three planes of existence, four modes of generation, five destinations, seven stations of consciousness, and nine abodes of beings—these are called 'states of being and so forth.' Among these states of being and so forth, for which resultant consciousnesses these formations are conditions, both at rebirth-linking and in the course of existence, and how they are conditions—this is how it should be understood; this is the meaning.

Tattha – puññābhisaṅkhāre tāva kāmāvacaraaṭṭhacetanābhedo puññābhisaṅkhāro avisesena kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ navannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena cāti dvidhā paccayo. Rūpāvacarapañcakusalacetanābhedo puññābhisaṅkhāro rūpabhave paṭisandhiyaṃ eva pañcannaṃ. Vuttappabhedakāmāvacaro pana kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ upekkhāsahagatāhetukamanoviññāṇadhātuvajjānaṃ sattannaṃ parittavipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva dvidhā paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Sveva rūpabhave pañcannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Kāmabhave pana duggatiyaṃ aṭṭhannampi parittavipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ.

Herein, as for meritorious formations: first, the meritorious formation comprising the eight types of sense-sphere wholesome volition is, without distinction, a condition in two ways—namely, by way of diverse-moment kamma-condition and by way of decisive-support condition—for the nine resultant consciousnesses at rebirth-linking in a happy destiny in the sense-sphere existence. The meritorious formation comprising the five types of form-sphere wholesome volition is a condition for the five resultant consciousnesses in the form-sphere existence at rebirth-linking only. The aforementioned type of sense-sphere meritorious formation, however, is a condition in the same two ways for the seven limited resultant consciousnesses (excluding the rootless mind-consciousness-element accompanied by equanimity) in a happy destiny in the sense-sphere existence during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. That same meritorious formation is similarly a condition for the five resultant consciousnesses in the form-sphere existence during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. But in an unhappy destiny in the sense-sphere existence, it is similarly a condition for all eight limited resultant consciousnesses during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking.

Tattha niraye mahāmoggallānattherassa narakacārikādīsu iṭṭhārammaṇasamāyoge so paccayo hoti. Tiracchānesu pana nāgasupaṇṇapetamahiddhikesu ca iṭṭhārammaṇaṃ labbhatiyeva. Sveva kāmabhave sugatiyaṃ soḷasannampi kusalavipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca. Avisesena puññābhisaṅkhāro rūpabhave dasannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca.

Therein, in hell, that condition occurs upon encountering a desirable object, as in the case of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna's wanderings in hell and so on. Among animals, however, a desirable object can certainly be obtained among nāgas, supaṇṇas, and powerful petas. That same meritorious formation is similarly a condition for all sixteen wholesome-resultant consciousnesses in a happy destiny in the sense-sphere existence, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking. Without distinction, the meritorious formation is a condition for the ten resultant consciousnesses in the form-sphere existence, similarly, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking.

Dvādasākusalacetanābhedo apuññābhisaṅkhāro kāmabhave duggatiyaṃ ekassa viññāṇassa tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatte; channaṃ pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ; sattannampi akusalavipākaviññāṇānaṃ pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca[M 0.0158]. Kāmabhave pana sugatiyaṃ tesaṃyeva sattannaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ; rūpabhave catunnaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. So ca kho kāmāvacare aniṭṭharūpadassanasaddasavanavasena[P 0.0167]. Brahmaloke pana aniṭṭhā rūpādayo nāma natthi, tathā kāmāvacaradevalokepi.

The demeritorious formation, comprising the twelve types of unwholesome volition, is similarly a condition in an unhappy destiny in the sense-sphere existence for one consciousness at rebirth-linking, but not during the course of existence; for six consciousnesses during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking; and for all seven types of unwholesome-resultant consciousness, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking. But in a happy destiny in the sense-sphere existence, it is similarly a condition for those same seven during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. In the form-sphere existence, it is similarly a condition for four types of resultant consciousness during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. And that, in the sense-sphere, is by way of seeing undesirable forms and hearing undesirable sounds. In the Brahma world, however, there are no such things as undesirable forms and so on; likewise in the sense-sphere deva worlds.

Āneñjābhisaṅkhāro [V 0.0158] arūpabhave catunnaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca.

The imperturbable formation is similarly a condition for the four resultant consciousnesses in the formless-sphere existence, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking.

Kāmāvacarakusalākusalato pana sabbasaṅgāhikanayena vīsaticetanābhedopi kāyasaṅkhāro kāmabhave dasannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena ceva upanissayapaccayena cāti dvidhā paccayo. Sveva kāmabhave terasannaṃ, rūpabhave navannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Sveva kāmabhave tevīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ca paṭisandhiyañca. Vacīsaṅkhārepi eseva nayo.

However, the bodily formation, which comprises twenty types of volition from the sense-sphere wholesome and unwholesome according to the all-inclusive method, is a condition for ten resultant consciousnesses at rebirth-linking in the sense-sphere existence in two ways: namely, by way of diverse-moment kamma-condition and by way of decisive-support condition. That same bodily formation is similarly a condition during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking, for thirteen resultant consciousnesses in the sense-sphere existence and for nine in the form-sphere existence. That same bodily formation is similarly a condition both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking for twenty-three resultant consciousnesses in the sense-sphere existence. This same method also applies to the verbal formation.

Aṭṭhavīsatiekūnatiṃsacetanābhedopi pana cittasaṅkhāro tīsu bhavesu ekūnavīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ, no pavatte. Sveva dvīsu bhavesu heṭṭhāvuttānaṃ terasannañca navannañcāti dvāvīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte, no paṭisandhiyaṃ. Tīsu pana bhavesu dvattiṃsāyapi vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo pavatte ceva paṭisandhiyañca. Evaṃ tāva bhavesu paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ vasena te saṅkhārā yesaṃ paccayā, yathā ca paccayā honti tathā vijānitabbā. Eteneva nayena yoniādīsupi veditabbā.

However, the mental formation, comprising twenty-eight or twenty-nine types of volition, is similarly a condition for nineteen resultant consciousnesses in the three kinds of existence at rebirth-linking, but not during the course of existence. That same mental formation is similarly a condition for twenty-two resultant consciousnesses—namely, the thirteen and the nine mentioned above—in two kinds of existence, during the course of existence, but not at rebirth-linking. But in the three kinds of existence, it is similarly a condition for all thirty-two resultant consciousnesses, both during the course of existence and at rebirth-linking. Thus, these formations should be understood according to the kinds of existence, by way of rebirth-linking and the course of existence, as to which they are a condition for, and how they are a condition. By this same method, they should be understood also in regard to the modes of birth and so on.

Tatridaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya mukhamattappakāsanaṃ – imesu hi saṅkhāresu yasmā puññābhisaṅkhāro tāva dvīsu bhavesu paṭisandhiṃ datvā sabbaṃ attano vipākaṃ janeti, tathā aṇḍajādīsu catūsu yonīsu, devamanussasaṅkhātāsu dvīsu gatīsu, nānattakāyanānattasaññīnānattakāyaekattasaññīekattakāyanānattasaññīekattakāyaekattasaññīsaṅkhātāsu manussānañceva paṭhamadutiyatatiyajjhānabhūmīnañca vasena catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu. Asaññasattāvāse panesa rūpamattamevābhisaṅkharotīti catūsuyeva sattāvāsesu ca paṭisandhiṃ datvā sabbaṃ attano vipākaṃ janeti. Tasmā esa [M 0.0159] etesu dvīsu bhavesu, catūsu yonīsu, dvīsu gatīsu, catūsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, catūsu [P 0.0168] sattāvāsesu ca ekavīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti yathāsambhavaṃ paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca.

Herein, this is a mere introductory explanation from the beginning: Among these formations, because the meritorious formation, having given rebirth in two kinds of existence, generates all its own result—similarly in the four modes of birth, in the two destinies designated as devas and humans, and in the four stations of consciousness (namely, beings with diverse bodies and diverse perceptions; beings with diverse bodies and uniform perception; beings with uniform body and diverse perceptions; and beings with uniform body and uniform perception, by way of humans and the first, second, and third jhānic planes); and because in the abode of non-percipient beings it forms only materiality—thus, having given rebirth in only four abodes of beings, it generates all its own result. Therefore, this formation is a condition for twenty-one resultant consciousnesses in these two kinds of existence, four modes of birth, two destinies, four stations of consciousness, and four abodes of beings, in the manner described, as is possible, at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence.

Apuññābhisaṅkhāro pana yasmā ekasmiññeva kāmabhave, catūsu yonīsu, avasesāsu tīsu gatīsu, nānattakāyaekattasaññīsaṅkhātāya ekissā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyā, tādiseyeva ca ekasmiṃ [V 0.0159] sattāvāse paṭisandhivasena vipaccati, tasmā esa ekasmiṃ bhave catūsu yonīsu, tīsu gatīsu, ekissā viññāṇaṭṭhitiyā, ekamhi ca sattāvāse sattannaṃ vipākaviññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca.

The demeritorious formation, however, because it ripens by way of rebirth-linking in only one sense-sphere existence, in the four modes of birth, in the remaining three destinies, in the one station of consciousness designated as 'beings with diverse bodies and uniform perception,' and in just such a single abode of beings; therefore, this formation is a condition for seven resultant consciousnesses in the manner described, in one kind of existence, four modes of birth, three destinies, one station of consciousness, and one abode of beings, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of existence.

Āneñjābhisaṅkhāro pana yasmā ekasmiṃ arūpabhave, ekissā opapātikayoniyā, ekissā devagatiyā, ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, ākāsānañcāyatanādīsu ca catūsu sattāvāsesu paṭisandhivasena vipaccati, tasmā esa ekasmiṃyeva bhave, ekissā yoniyā, ekissā devagatiyā, tīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu catūsu sattāvāsesu, catunnaṃ viññāṇānaṃ vuttanayeneva paccayo hoti paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca.

The imperturbable volitional formation, since it ripens by way of rebirth in one formless plane of existence, in one spontaneous mode of generation, in one divine destiny, in the three stations of consciousness beginning with the base of the infinity of space, and in the four abodes of beings beginning with the base of the infinity of space, therefore, this formation is a condition for four consciousnesses in the manner described, in one plane of existence only, one mode of generation, one divine destiny, three stations of consciousness, and four abodes of beings, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of life.

Kāyasaṅkhāropi yasmā ekasmiṃ kāmabhave, catūsu yonīsu, pañcasu gatīsu, dvīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, dvīsu ca sattāvāsesu paṭisandhiṃ datvā sabbaṃ attano vipākaṃ janeti, tasmā esa ekasmiṃ bhave, catūsu yonīsu, pañcasu gatīsu, dvīsu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, dvīsu ca sattāvāsesu tevīsatiyā vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca. Vacīsaṅkhārepi eseva nayo.

The bodily volitional formation also, because in one sensual plane of existence, in four modes of generation, in five destinies, in two stations of consciousness, and in two abodes of beings, it gives rebirth-linking and generates all its own results, therefore, this formation is a condition for twenty-three resultant consciousnesses in the same manner, in one plane of existence, four modes of generation, five destinies, two stations of consciousness, and two abodes of beings, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of life. The same principle applies to the verbal volitional formation.

Cittasaṅkhāro pana yasmā ekaṃ sattāvāsaṃ ṭhapetvā na katthaci na vipaccati, tasmā esa tīsu bhavesu, catūsu yonīsu, pañcasu gatīsu, sattasu viññāṇaṭṭhitīsu, aṭṭhasu sattāvāsesu yathāyogaṃ dvattiṃsāya vipākaviññāṇānaṃ tatheva paccayo paṭisandhiyaṃ pavatte ca. Aviññāṇake pana sattāvāse saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ natthi.

The mental volitional formation, because, with the exception of one abode of beings, it ripens everywhere, therefore, this formation is a condition for thirty-two resultant consciousnesses in the same manner, in the three planes of existence, four modes of generation, five destinies, seven stations of consciousness, and eight abodes of beings, as appropriate, both at rebirth-linking and during the course of life. However, in the abode of non-percipient beings, there is no consciousness conditioned by volitional formations.

Apica puññābhisaṅkhāro asaññasattesu kaṭattārūpānaṃ nānākkhaṇikakammapaccayena paccayoti. Evaṃ –

Moreover, the wholesome volitional formation is a condition for kamma-born materiality in non-percipient beings by way of the diverse-moment kamma condition. Thus:

Paṭisandhipavattīnaṃ[M 0.0160], vasenete bhavādisu;

Vijānitabbā saṅkhārā, yathā yesañca paccayāti.

By way of rebirth-linking and the course of life, / these formations should be understood / in planes of existence and so on, / and for what they are conditions.

Saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇapadaniddeso.

The Exposition of 'Consciousness Conditioned by Formations'.

Nāmarūpapadaniddeso

Exposition of the Term 'Name-and-Form'

228. Viññāṇapaccayā [P 0.0169][V 0.0160] nāmarūpaniddese –

228. In the exposition of 'name-and-form conditioned by consciousness'—

Desanābhedato sabba-bhavādīsu pavattito;

Saṅgahā paccayanayā, viññātabbo vinicchayo.

The analysis should be understood: by way of distinctions in teaching, by its occurrence in all planes of existence and so on, by way of inclusion, and by the method of conditions.

‘Desanābhedato’ti “tattha katamaṃ rūpaṃ? Cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpa”nti (saṃ. ni. 2.2; ma. ni. 1.100) evaṃ tāva suttante ca idha rūpapadassa abhedato ekasadisā desanā katā; nāmapadassa pana bhedato.

‘By way of distinction in teaching’—thus, first, in the Suttanta and here, the teaching of the term ‘form’ is made without distinction, being uniform; but for the term ‘name’, it is with distinction.

Suttantasmiñhi “tattha katamaṃ nāmaṃ? Vedanā saññā cetanā phasso manasikāro”ti vuttaṃ. Idha “vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho”ti. Tattha hi yampi cakkhuviññāṇapaccayā nāmaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca cittassa ṭhiti arūpīnaṃ dhammānaṃ āyūti evaṃ aññadhammasannissayena aggahetabbato pākaṭaṃ, taṃ dassento cetanāphassamanasikāravasena saṅkhārakkhandhaṃ tidhā bhinditvā dvīhi khandhehi saddhiṃ desesi. Idha pana tattha vuttañca avuttañca sabbaṃ nāmaṃ saṅgaṇhanto “tayo khandhā – vedanākkhandho saññākkhandho saṅkhārakkhandho”ti āha.
