In the same way, the path neither abandons defilements divided as past, future, or present, nor does it not abandon them. For those defilements that would arise in the aggregates if they were not fully understood, once the path has arisen and the aggregates are fully understood, those defilements, being unborn, do not come to be born; being unproduced, do not come to be produced; being unmanifested, do not become manifest. This meaning should also be illustrated by the example of medicine taken by a young mother to prevent another birth, or by the sick for the pacification of a disease. Thus, concerning the defilements that the path abandons, it cannot be said that they are past, future, or present. And yet, the path does not fail to abandon defilements. It is with reference to the defilements that the path abandons that it is said, ‘of arisen evil states,’ and so on.

Na kevalañca maggo kileseyeva pajahati, kilesānaṃ pana appahīnattā ye uppajjeyyuṃ upādinnakkhandhā, tepi pajahatiyeva. Vuttampi cetaṃ “sotāpattimaggañāṇena abhisaṅkhāraviññāṇassa nirodhena satta bhave ṭhapetvā anamatagge saṃsāre ye uppajjeyyuṃ nāmañca rūpañca etthete nirujjhantī”ti (cūḷani. ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa 6) vitthāro. Iti maggo upādinnato anupādinnato ca vuṭṭhāti. Bhavavasena pana sotāpattimaggo apāyabhavato vuṭṭhāti[V 0.0285]. Sakadāgāmimaggo sugatibhavekadesato; anāgāmimaggo sugatikāmabhavato; vuṭṭhāti arahattamaggo rūpārūpabhavato vuṭṭhāti, sabbabhavehi vuṭṭhātiyevātipi vadanti.

Not only does the path abandon the defilements, but it also abandons the clung-to aggregates that would arise from the non-abandonment of the defilements. As it is said: “Through the knowledge of the path of stream-entry, with the cessation of consciousness resulting from volitional formations, setting aside seven existences, whatever name-and-form would arise in the beginningless round of rebirth—these cease right here.” Thus, the path emerges from both the clung-to and the not-clung-to. In terms of existence, the path of stream-entry emerges from the plane of misery. The path of once-returning emerges from a part of the fortunate planes of existence. The path of non-returning emerges from the fortunate sensual plane of existence. The path of arahantship emerges from the form and formless planes of existence; some say it emerges from all existences whatsoever.

Atha maggakkhaṇe kathaṃ anuppannānaṃ uppādāya bhāvanā hoti? Kathaṃ vā uppannānaṃ ṭhitiyāti? Maggappavattiyā eva. Maggo hi pavattamāno pubbe anuppannapubbattā anuppanno nāma vuccati. Anāgatapubbañhi ṭhānaṃ gantvā ananubhūtapubbaṃ vā ārammaṇaṃ anubhavitvā vattāro bhavanti – ‘anāgataṭṭhānaṃ āgatamha, ananubhūtaṃ ārammaṇaṃ anubhavāmā’ti. Yā cassa pavatti, ayameva ṭhiti nāmāti ṭhitiyā bhāvetīti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Evametassa bhikkhuno idaṃ lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe vīriyaṃ “anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāyā”tiādīni [M 0.0288] cattāri nāmāni labhati. Ayaṃ lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe sammappadhānakathā. Evamettha lokiyalokuttaramissakā sammappadhānā niddiṭṭhāti.

Then, at the moment of the path, how is there development for the arising of what has not yet arisen? Or how for the stability of what has already arisen? It is by the very occurrence of the path. For the path, as it occurs, is called ‘that which is unarisen’ because it has never arisen before. Indeed, having gone to a place never gone to before, or having experienced an object never experienced before, people say, ‘We have come to a place never before reached; we are experiencing an object never before experienced.’ And its very occurrence is called ‘stability’; thus it is fitting to say that one develops for stability. In this way, for this bhikkhu, at the moment of the supramundane path, this effort obtains the four names beginning with ‘for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen.’ This is the discourse on right exertion at the moment of the supramundane path. Thus, the right exertions, a mixture of the mundane and supramundane, have here been explained.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Exposition of the Suttas.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Exposition

408. Abhidhammabhājanīye sabbānipi sammappadhānāni dhammasaṅgaṇiyaṃ vibhattassa desanānayassa mukhamattameva dassentena niddiṭṭhāni. Tattha nayabhedo veditabbo. Kathaṃ? Paṭhamasammappadhāne [P 0.0302] tāva sotāpattimagge jhānābhinivese suddhikapaṭipadā, suddhikasuññatā, suññatapaṭipadā, suddhikaappaṇihitā, appaṇihitapaṭipadāti imesu pañcasu ṭhānesu dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ catukkapañcakanayānaṃ vasena dasa nayā honti. Evaṃ sesesupīti vīsatiyā abhinivesesu dve nayasatāni. Tāni catūhi adhipatīhi catugguṇitāni aṭṭha. Iti suddhikāni dve sādhipatīni aṭṭhāti sabbampi nayasahassaṃ hoti. Tathādutiyasammappadhānādīsu suddhikasammappadhāne cāti sotāpattimagge pañcanayasahassāni. Yathā ca sotāpattimagge, evaṃ sesamaggesupīti kusalavaseneva vīsati nayasahassāni. Vipāke pana sammappadhānehi kattabbakiccaṃ [V 0.0286] natthīti vipākavāro na gahitoti. Sammappadhānāni panettha nibbattitalokuttarāneva kathitānīti veditabbāni.

408. In the Abhidhamma Division, all the right efforts are set forth merely to show an introduction to the method of teaching analyzed in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī. Herein, the distinction of methods should be understood. How? First, in the initial right effort, regarding the path of stream-entry, in the five instances—the practice of purification, purified emptiness, the practice of emptiness, the purified signless, and the practice of the signless—there are ten methods by way of the fourfold and fivefold methods, two for each instance. Thus, for the remaining instances as well, there are two hundred methods across the twenty adherences. These, multiplied by the four dominants, become eight hundred. Thus, the two hundred pure methods and the eight hundred with dominants make a total of one thousand methods. Similarly, for the second right effort and so on, and for the pure right effort, there are five thousand methods on the path of stream-entry. As it is for the path of stream-entry, so it is for the remaining paths, making twenty thousand methods in the wholesome sphere. However, since there is no function to be performed by resultant right efforts, the section on the resultant is not included. It should be understood that the right efforts spoken of here are exclusively those that have produced the supramundane.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division.

3. Pañhāpucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Questioning Section

427. Pañhāpucchake pāḷianusāreneva sammappadhānānaṃ kusalādibhāvo veditabbo. Ārammaṇattikesu pana sabbānipi etāni appamāṇaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha pavattito appamāṇārammaṇāneva, na maggārammaṇāni; sahajātahetuvasena pana maggahetukāni; vīmaṃsaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā maggabhāvanākāle [M 0.0289] maggādhipatīni; chandacittajeṭṭhikāya maggabhāvanāya na vattabbāni maggādhipatīnīti; vīriyajeṭṭhikāya pana aññassa vīriyassa abhāvā na vattabbāni maggādhipatīnīti vā na maggādhipatīnīti vā; atītādīsu ekārammaṇabhāvenapi na vattabbāni; nibbānassa pana bahiddhādhammattā bahiddhārammaṇāni nāma hontīti. Evametasmiṃ pañhāpucchake nibbattitalokuttarāneva sammappadhānāni kathitāni. Sammāsambuddhena hi suttantabhājanīyasmiṃyeva lokiyalokuttaramissakā sammappadhānā kathitā; abhidhammabhājanīyapañhāpucchakesu pana lokuttarāyevāti. Evamayaṃ sammappadhānavibhaṅgopi teparivaṭṭaṃ nīharitvāva bhājetvā dassitoti.

427. In the Questioning Section, the wholesome and other qualities of the right efforts should be understood according to the sequence of the Pāli text. In the triads of objects, all these are immeasurable-object states since they arise having the immeasurable Nibbāna as their object, not path-object states; however, they are path-rooted by way of the co-nascence condition. During the development of the path, with investigation as the principal factor, they are path-dominants; with zeal and consciousness as the principal factors in the development of the path, they cannot be called path-dominants; in the case where energy is the principal factor, due to the absence of another energy, they are likewise not to be called path-dominants. Also, they cannot be spoken of as having a single object in the past, etc.; but since Nibbāna is an external phenomenon, they are called external-object states. Thus, in this Questioning Section, only right efforts that have produced the supramundane are discussed. For the Fully Enlightened One taught mixed mundane and supramundane right efforts in the Sutta Division, but in the Abhidhamma Division and the Questioning Sections, only the supramundane. Thus, this analysis of the right efforts is shown after extracting and dividing it according to the three rounds.

Sammohavinodaniyā vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāya

From the Sammohavinodanī, the Commentary on the Vibhaṅga

Sammappadhānavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of Right Efforts is concluded.

9. Iddhipādavibhaṅgo

9. Analysis of the Bases of Power

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Sutta Division

431. Idāni [P 0.0303][M 0.0290][V 0.0287] tadanantare iddhipādavibhaṅge cattāroti gaṇanaparicchedo. Iddhipādāti ettha ijjhatīti iddhi, samijjhati nipphajjatīti attho. Ijjhanti vā etāya sattā iddhā vuddhā ukkaṃsagatā hontītipi iddhi. Paṭhamenatthena iddhi eva pādo iddhipādo, iddhikoṭṭhāsoti attho. Dutiyenatthena iddhiyā pādoti iddhipādo; pādoti patiṭṭhā, adhigamupāyoti attho. Tena hi yasmā uparūparivisesasaṅkhātaṃ iddhiṃ pajjanti pāpuṇanti, tasmā pādoti vuccati. Evaṃ tāva “cattāro iddhipādā”ti ettha attho veditabbo.

431. Now, immediately following, in the Analysis of the Bases of Power, the enumeration is “four.” Here, in the term iddhipāda: “It succeeds” (ijjhati) is iddhi (power); it accomplishes, it is achieved—this is the meaning. Or alternatively, beings succeed (ijjhanti) by this, become powerful (iddhā), developed, and exalted—thus also it is iddhi. In the first sense, power itself is the basis (pādo); iddhipāda means a component of power. In the second sense, it is the basis for power (iddhiyā pādo); here, pāda means foundation, the means of attainment. Therefore, because they lead to and attain power, which is characterized by higher and higher distinctions, it is called pāda, a “basis.” Thus, first, the meaning of “the four bases of power” should be understood in this way.

Idāni te bhājetvā dassetuṃ idha bhikkhūtiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha idha bhikkhūti imasmiṃ sāsane bhikkhu. Chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgatanti ettha chandahetuko chandādhiko vā samādhi chandasamādhi. Kattukamyatāchandaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhissetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Padhānabhūtā saṅkhārā padhānasaṅkhārā. Catukiccasādhakassa sammappadhānavīriyassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Samannāgatanti chandasamādhinā ca padhānasaṅkhārehi ca upetaṃ. Iddhipādanti nipphattipariyāyena vā ijjhanakaṭṭhena ijjhanti etāya sattā iddhā vuddhā ukkaṃsagatā hontīti iminā vā pariyāyena iddhīti saṅkhaṃ gatānaṃ upacārajjhānādikusalacittasampayuttānaṃ chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārānaṃ adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena pādabhūtaṃ sesacittacetasikarāsinti attho. Yañhi parato “iddhipādoti tathābhūtassa vedanākkhandho…pe… viññāṇakkhandho”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ iminā atthena yujjati. Iminā nayena sesesupi attho veditabbo. Yatheva hi chandaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhi [P 0.0304] chandasamādhīti [V 0.0288] vutto, evaṃ vīriyaṃ…pe… cittaṃ. Vīmaṃsaṃ adhipatiṃ karitvā paṭiladdhasamādhi vīmaṃsasamādhīti vuccati.

Now, to explain these by analyzing them, the passage beginning "Here, a bhikkhu..." is introduced. In this context, "here, a bhikkhu" refers to a bhikkhu in this dispensation. In the phrase "endowed with desire-concentration and the volitional formations of striving" (chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgata): here, concentration that is caused by desire or has desire as its dominant factor is called "desire-concentration" (chandasamādhi). This is a term for the concentration attained by making the desire to act the dominant factor. The volitional formations that constitute striving are called "the volitional formations of striving" (padhānasaṅkhārā). This is a term for the energy of right effort that accomplishes the fourfold task. "Endowed" means possessing both desire-concentration and the volitional formations of striving. The term 'basis of power' (iddhipāda) refers to the entire complex of wholesome consciousness and mental factors, which has as its foundation (pādabhūtaṃ) the desire-concentration and volitional formations of striving. These foundational factors, associated with wholesome consciousness such as access jhāna, are designated as 'power' (iddhi) either in the sense of accomplishment or in the sense that 'beings succeed through this, becoming powerful, developed, and exalted.' For what is stated elsewhere—"The basis of power is the feeling aggregate... the consciousness aggregate of one who is thus"—is consistent with this meaning. By this method, the meaning should be understood in the remaining cases as well. Just as concentration attained by making desire the dominant factor is called "desire-concentration," so too concentration attained by making energy... mind... or investigation the dominant factor is called "energy-concentration"... "mind-concentration"... or "investigation-concentration," respectively.

Idāni chandasamādhiādīni padāni bhājetvā dassetuṃ kathañca bhikkhūtiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha chandañce bhikkhu adhipatiṃ karitvāti yadi bhikkhu chandaṃ adhipatiṃ chandaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ chandaṃ dhuraṃ chandaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā samādhiṃ paṭilabhati nibbatteti, evaṃ nibbattito ayaṃ samādhi chandasamādhi nāma vuccatīti attho. Vīriyañcetiādīsupi [M 0.0291] eseva nayo. Ime vuccanti padhānasaṅkhārāti ettāvatā chandiddhipādaṃ bhāvayamānassa bhikkhuno padhānābhisaṅkhārasaṅkhātacatukiccasādhakaṃ vīriyaṃ kathitaṃ. Tadekajjhaṃ abhisaññūhitvāti taṃ sabbaṃ ekato rāsiṃ katvāti attho. Saṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti etaṃ vohāraṃ gacchatīti veditabbanti attho.

Now, to explain the terms 'desire-concentration' and so on by analyzing them, the passage beginning, 'And how, bhikkhu...' is introduced. Herein, 'if a bhikkhu makes desire the dominant factor' means that if a bhikkhu attains and produces concentration by making desire the dominant factor, the chief, the yoke, and the forerunner, then this concentration, thus produced, is called 'desire-concentration.' The same method applies to the phrases beginning 'energy...' and so on. 'These are called the formations of striving'—by this much is explained the energy that accomplishes the fourfold task, known as the volitional formation of striving, for a bhikkhu developing the basis of spiritual power of desire. 'Having amassed them together' means gathering them all into one mass. 'It goes to reckoning'—this should be understood as 'it enters into conventional designation.'

433. Idāni “chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhāro”ti etasmiṃ padasamūhe chandādidhamme bhājetvā dassetuṃ tattha katamo chandotiādi āraddhaṃ. Taṃ uttānatthameva.

433. Now, to explain the phrase 'chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhāro' by analyzing the constituent states such as desire and so on, the passage beginning, 'Herein, what is desire?' is introduced. Its meaning is quite clear.

Upeto hotīti iddhipādasaṅkhāto dhammarāsi upeto hoti. Tesaṃ dhammānanti tesaṃ sampayuttānaṃ chandādidhammānaṃ. Iddhi samiddhītiādīni sabbāni nipphattivevacanāneva. Evaṃ santepi ijjhanakaṭṭhena iddhi. Sampuṇṇā iddhi samiddhi; upasaggena vā padaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ. Ijjhanākāro ijjhanā. Samijjhanāti upasaggena padaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ. Attano santāne pātubhāvavasena labhanaṃ lābho. Parihīnānampi vīriyārambhavasena puna lābho paṭilābho; upasaggena vā padaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ. Pattīti adhigamo. Aparihānavasena sammā pattīti sampatti. Phusanāti paṭilābhaphusanā. Sacchikiriyāti [P 0.0305] paṭilābhasacchikiriyāva. Upasampadāti paṭilābhaupasampadā evāti veditabbā.

He is endowed—that is, he is endowed with the mass of states termed the bases of spiritual power. 'Of those states'—of those associated states such as desire and so on. 'Spiritual power, success,' and so on—all these are simply terms denoting accomplishment. Even so, 'iddhi' (spiritual power) is iddhi in the sense of succeeding. 'Samiddhi' (complete success) is complete iddhi; or the word is augmented by a prefix. 'Ijjhanā' is the mode of succeeding. 'Samijjhanā' is the word augmented by a prefix. 'Lābha' (gain) is obtaining by way of manifestation in one's own continuity. 'Paṭilābha' (attainment) is gaining again through initiating effort even after decline; or the word is augmented by a prefix. 'Patti' (attainment) is achievement. 'Sampatti' (success) is right attainment by way of non-decline. 'Phusanā' (touching) is the touching of attainment. 'Sacchikiriyā' (realization) is simply the realization of attainment. 'Upasampadā' (full acquisition) should be understood as simply the full acquisition of attainment.

Tayābhūtassāti tena ākārena bhūtassa; te chandādidhamme paṭilabhitvā ṭhitassāti attho. Vedanākkhandhotiādīhi chandādayo anto katvā cattāropi khandhā kathitā. Te dhammeti te cattāro arūpakkhandhe; chandādayo vā tayo dhammetipi vuttaṃ. Āsevatītiādīni vuttatthāneva. Sesaiddhipādaniddesesupi imināva nayena attho veditabbo.

'Of one who has become thus'—of one who has become so in that way; the meaning is, of one who stands firm, having obtained those states of desire and so on. 'The aggregate of feeling,' etc.—by including desire and so on, all four aggregates are discussed. 'Those states'—those four formless aggregates; or it is also said, 'those three states,' desire and so on. 'He cultivates,' etc., have the meaning as stated. In the expositions of the remaining bases of spiritual power, the meaning should be understood in the same way.

Ettāvatā [V 0.0289] kiṃ kathitanti? Catunnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ matthakappattaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ kathitaṃ. Eko hi bhikkhu chandaṃ avassayati; kattukamyatākusaladhammacchandena atthanipphattiyaṃ sati ‘ahaṃ lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattessāmi, natthi mayhaṃ etassa nibbattane bhāro’ti chandaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ chandaṃ dhuraṃ chandaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbatteti. Eko vīriyaṃ avassayati. Eko cittaṃ, eko paññaṃ avassayati. Paññāya atthanipphattiyaṃ sati ‘ahaṃ lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattessāmi[M 0.0292], natthi mayhaṃ etassa nibbattane bhāro’ti paññaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ paññaṃ dhuraṃ paññaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbatteti.

What has been said thus far? The meditation subject that has reached the pinnacle for four bhikkhus has been discussed. For one bhikkhu relies on desire; when there is the fulfillment of purpose through the desire for wholesome states and the wish to act, thinking, 'I will produce the supramundane Dhamma; there is no burden for me in producing it,' he makes desire the chief, the yoke, the forerunner, and produces the supramundane Dhamma. Another relies on energy. Another relies on mind. Another relies on wisdom. When there is the fulfillment of purpose through wisdom, thinking, 'I will produce the supramundane Dhamma; there is no burden for me in producing it,' he makes wisdom the chief, the yoke, the forerunner, and produces the supramundane Dhamma.

Kathaṃ? Yathā hi catūsu amaccaputtesu ṭhānantaraṃ patthetvā vicarantesu eko upaṭṭhānaṃ avassayi, eko sūrabhāvaṃ, eko jātiṃ, eko mantaṃ. Kathaṃ? Tesu hi paṭhamo ‘upaṭṭhāne appamādakāritāya atthanipphattiyā sati labbhamānaṃ lacchāmetaṃ ṭhānantara’nti upaṭṭhānaṃ avassayi. Dutiyo ‘upaṭṭhāne appamattopi ekacco saṅgāme paccupaṭṭhite saṇṭhātuṃ na sakkoti; avassaṃ kho pana rañño paccanto kuppissati; tasmiṃ kuppite rathadhure kammaṃ katvā rājānaṃ ārādhetvā āharāpessāmetaṃ ṭhānantara’nti sūrabhāvaṃ avassayi. Tatiyo ‘sūrabhāvepi sati ekacco hīnajātiko hoti; jātiṃ sodhetvā ṭhānantaraṃ dadantā mayhaṃ dassantī’ti jātiṃ avassayi. Catuttho ‘jātimāpi eko amantanīyo hoti; mantena kattabbakicce uppanne āharāpessāmetaṃ ṭhānantara’nti mantaṃ [P 0.0306] avassayi. Te sabbepi attano attano avassayabalena ṭhānantarāni pāpuṇiṃsu.

How? It is as when four sons of ministers were seeking a position: one relied on attendance, one on heroism, one on birth, and one on counsel. How so? Among them, the first relied on attendance, thinking, 'Through diligent attendance, when the purpose is accomplished, I will obtain this obtainable position.' The second relied on heroism, thinking, 'Even if one is diligent in attendance, some cannot stand firm when battle arises. Surely the king's border will revolt; when it does, by performing my duty at the chariot-pole and pleasing the king, I will have him grant me this position.' The third relied on birth, thinking, 'Even if one is heroic, some are of low birth. When they grant a position after verifying one's lineage, they will give it to me.' The fourth relied on counsel, thinking, 'Even one of high birth may be unfit for counsel. When a task to be done by counsel arises, I will have him grant me this position.' All of them, through the strength of their respective reliance, attained their positions.

Tattha upaṭṭhāne appamatto hutvā ṭhānantaraṃ patto viya chandaṃ avassāya kattukamyatākusaladhammacchandena atthanibbattiyaṃ sati ‘ahaṃ lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattessāmi, natthi mayhaṃ etassa nibbattane bhāro’ti chandaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ chandaṃ dhuraṃ chandaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā lokuttaradhammanibbattako daṭṭhabbo, raṭṭhapālatthero (ma. ni. 2.293 ādayo) viya. So hi āyasmā chandaṃ dhuraṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattesi. Sūrabhāvena rājānaṃ ārādhetvā ṭhānantaraṃ patto viya vīriyaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ vīriyaṃ dhuraṃ vīriyaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā lokuttaradhammanibbattako daṭṭhabbo, soṇatthero (mahāva. 243) viya. So hi āyasmā vīriyaṃ dhuraṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattesi.

Herein, like one who attained a position by being diligent in attendance, so should be seen the producer of the supramundane Dhamma who, relying on desire, when the goal is accomplished through the desire for wholesome states and the wish to act, thinks, ‘I will produce the supramundane Dhamma; there is no burden for me in producing it,’ and makes desire the chief, the yoke, and the forerunner—as in the case of the Elder Raṭṭhapāla (MN 2.293 ff.). For that venerable one made desire his yoke and produced the supramundane Dhamma. And like one who attained a position by pleasing the king through bravery, so should be seen the producer of the supramundane Dhamma who makes energy the chief, the yoke, and the forerunner—as in the case of the Elder Soṇa (Mahāvagga 243). For that venerable one made energy his yoke and produced the supramundane Dhamma.

Jātisampattiyā [V 0.0290] ṭhānantaraṃ patto viya cittaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ cittaṃ dhuraṃ cittaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā lokuttaradhammanibbattako daṭṭhabbo, sambhūtatthero viya. So hi āyasmā cittaṃ dhuraṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattesi. Mantaṃ avassāya ṭhānantarappatto viya vīmaṃsaṃ jeṭṭhakaṃ vīmaṃsaṃ dhuraṃ vīmaṃsaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ katvā [M 0.0293] lokuttaradhammanibbattako daṭṭhabbo, thero mogharājā viya. So hi āyasmā vīmaṃsaṃ dhuraṃ katvā lokuttaradhammaṃ nibbattesi.

Just as one who has attained a higher status through excellence of birth should be seen as a generator of the supramundane Dhamma by making the mind pre-eminent, the mind the mainstay, the mind the forerunner—like the Elder Sambhūta. For that venerable one made the mind the mainstay and generated the supramundane Dhamma. Just as one who has attained a higher status by relying on counsel should be seen as a generator of the supramundane Dhamma by making investigation pre-eminent, investigation the mainstay, investigation the forerunner—like the Elder Mogharājā. For that venerable one made investigation the mainstay and generated the supramundane Dhamma.

Ettha ca tayo chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasaṅkhātā dhammā iddhīpi honti iddhipādāpi. Sesā pana sampayuttakā cattāro khandhā iddhipādāyeva. Vīriyacittavīmaṃsasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasaṅkhātāpi tayo dhammā iddhīpi honti iddhipādāpi. Sesā pana sampayuttakā cattāro khandhā iddhipādāyeva. Ayaṃ tāva abhedato kathā.

Here, the three states designated as zeal, concentration, and the formations of striving are both powers and bases of power. The remaining four associated aggregates are solely bases of power. Similarly, the three states in the cases of energy, mind, and investigation, along with concentration and the formations of striving, are also both powers and bases of power. The remaining four associated aggregates are solely bases of power. This, for now, is the discussion without distinction.

Bhedato pana ‘chando’ iddhi nāma. Chandadhurena bhāvitā cattāro khandhā chandiddhipādo nāma. Samādhi padhānasaṅkhāroti dve dhammā saṅkhārakkhandhavasena chandiddhipāde pavisanti; pāde paviṭṭhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Tattheva ‘samādhi’ iddhi nāma. Samādhidhurena bhāvitā cattāro khandhā samādhiddhipādo nāma. Chando [P 0.0307] padhānasaṅkhāroti dve dhammā saṅkhārakkhandhavasena samādhiddhipāde pavisanti; pāde paviṭṭhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati eva. Tattheva ‘padhānasaṅkhāro’ iddhi nāma. Padhānasaṅkhārabhāvitā cattāro khandhā padhānasaṅkhāriddhipādo nāma. Chando samādhīti dve dhammā saṅkhārakkhandhavasena padhānasaṅkhāriddhipāde pavisanti; pāde paviṭṭhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati eva. Tattheva ‘vīriyaṃ’ iddhi nāma, ‘cittaṃ’ iddhi nāma, ‘vīmaṃsā’ iddhi nāma…pe… pāde paviṭṭhātipi vattuṃ vaṭṭati eva. Ayaṃ bhedato kathā nāma.

Now, with distinction, 'zeal' is called power. The four aggregates developed with zeal as the dominant factor are called the basis of power of zeal. Concentration and the formations of striving—these two states enter the basis of power of zeal by way of the aggregate of formations. It is also fitting to say that they are included in the basis. In the same way, 'concentration' is called power. The four aggregates developed with concentration as the dominant factor are called the basis of power of concentration. Zeal and the formations of striving—these two states enter the basis of power of concentration by way of the aggregate of formations. It is also fitting to say that they are included in the basis. Likewise, 'the formations of striving' is called power. The four aggregates developed with the formations of striving as the dominant factor are called the basis of power of the formations of striving. Zeal and concentration—these two states enter the basis of power of the formations of striving by way of the aggregate of formations. It is also fitting to say that they are included in the basis. In the same way, 'energy' is called power, 'mind' is called power, 'investigation' is called power... and so on... It is also fitting to say that they are included in the basis. This is called the discussion with distinction.

Ettha pana abhinavaṃ natthi; gahitameva vibhūtadhātukaṃ kataṃ. Kathaṃ? Chando, samādhi, padhānasaṅkhāroti ime tayo dhammā iddhīpi honti iddhipādāpi. Sesā sampayuttakā cattāro khandhā iddhipādāyeva. Ime hi tayo dhammā ijjhamānā sampayuttakehi catūhi khandhehi saddhiṃyeva ijjhanti, na vinā. Sampayuttakā pana cattāro khandhā ijjhanakaṭṭhena iddhi nāma honti, patiṭṭhānaṭṭhena pādo nāma. ‘Iddhī’ti vā ‘iddhipādo’ti vā na aññassa kassaci adhivacanaṃ, sampayuttakānaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃyeva adhivacanaṃ. Vīriyaṃ, cittaṃ, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhāroti tayo dhammā…pe… catunnaṃ khandhānaṃyeva adhivacanaṃ.

Here, however, there is nothing new; what has been taken has merely been made clear as to its components. How so? Zeal, concentration, and the formations of striving—these three states are both powers and bases of power. The remaining associated four aggregates are only bases of power. For these three states, when they succeed, they succeed only together with the four associated aggregates, not without them. The four associated aggregates, in the sense of accomplishing, are called 'power,' and in the sense of being a foundation, are called 'base.' The terms 'power' or 'base of power' are not designations for anything else; they are merely designations for the four associated aggregates. In the cases of energy, mind, and investigation, the three states... [the same applies, and these] are merely designations for the four aggregates.

Apica [V 0.0291] pubbabhāgo pubbabhāgo iddhipādo nāma; paṭilābho paṭilābho iddhi nāmāti veditabbo. Ayamattho upacārena vā vipassanāya vā dīpetabbo. Paṭhamajjhānaparikammañhi iddhipādo nāma, paṭhamajjhānaṃ iddhi nāma. Dutiyatatiyacatutthaākāsānañcāyatana, viññāṇañcāyatanaākiñcaññāyatananevasaññānāsaññāyatanaparikammaṃ [M 0.0294] iddhipādo nāma, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ iddhi nāma. Sotāpattimaggassa vipassanā iddhipādo nāma, sotāpattimaggo iddhi nāma. Sakadāgāmi, anāgāmi, arahattamaggassa vipassanā iddhipādo nāma, arahattamaggo iddhi nāma. Paṭilābhenāpi dīpetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Paṭhamajjhānañhi iddhipādo nāma, dutiyajjhānaṃ iddhi nāma; dutiyajjhānaṃ iddhipādo nāma, tatiyajjhānaṃ iddhi nāma…pe… anāgāmimaggo iddhipādo nāma, arahattamaggo iddhi nāma.

Furthermore, each preliminary part is called the 'base of power,' while each attainment is to be known as 'power.' This meaning should be explained either by way of proximity or by way of insight. The preliminary work for the first jhāna is called the 'base of power,' while the first jhāna is called 'power.' The preparatory work for the second, third, and fourth jhānas, the base of infinite space, the base of infinite consciousness, the base of nothingness, and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is called the 'base of power,' while the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is called 'power.' The insight for the path of stream-entry is called the 'base of power,' while the path of stream-entry is called 'power.' The insight for the paths of the once-returner, non-returner, and arahant is called the 'base of power,' while the path of the arahant is called 'power.' It is also fitting to explain this by way of attainment. The first jhāna is called the 'base of power,' while the second jhāna is called 'power'; the second jhāna is called the 'base of power,' while the third jhāna is called 'power'... the path of the non-returner is called the 'base of power,' while the path of the arahant is called 'power.'

Kenaṭṭhena [P 0.0308] iddhi? Kenaṭṭhena pādoti? Ijjhanakaṭṭheneva iddhi. Patiṭṭhānaṭṭheneva pādo. Evamidhāpi iddhīti vā pādoti vā na aññassa kassaci adhivacanaṃ, sampayuttakānaṃ catunnaṃ khandhānaṃyeva adhivacananti. Evaṃ vutte pana idamāhaṃsu – catunnaṃ khandhānameva adhivacanaṃ bhaveyya, yadi satthā parato uttaracūḷabhājanīyaṃ nāma na āhareyya. Uttaracūḷabhājanīye pana “chandoyeva chandiddhipādo, vīriyameva, cittameva, vīmaṃsāva vīmaṃsiddhipādo”ti kathitaṃ. Keci pana “iddhi nāma anipphannā, iddhipādo nipphanno”ti vadiṃsu. Tesaṃ vacanaṃ paṭikkhipitvā iddhīpi iddhipādopi ‘nipphanno tilakkhaṇabbhāhato’ti sanniṭṭhānaṃ kataṃ. Iti imasmiṃ suttantabhājanīye lokiyalokuttaramissakā iddhipādā kathitāti.

In what sense is there 'power'? In what sense is there a 'base'? It is 'power' in the sense of accomplishing, and a 'base' in the sense of foundation. Thus, here too, the terms 'power' or 'base' are not designations for anything else; they are merely designations for the four associated aggregates. When this was said, some then said: 'It would be a designation for the four aggregates alone, if the Teacher had not subsequently introduced the section named the Further Minor Analysis.' But in the Further Minor Analysis, it is stated: 'Zeal itself is the basis of power of zeal; energy itself is the basis of power of energy; mind itself is the basis of power of mind; investigation itself is the basis of power of investigation.' Some, however, said: 'Power is unproduced, while the base of power is produced.' Rejecting their statement, the conclusion was reached that both power and the base of power are 'produced, assailed by the three characteristics.' Thus, in this Suttanta Division, bases of power that are a mixture of mundane and supramundane are discussed.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Suttanta Division.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Division.

444. Abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ uttānatthameva. Nayā panettha gaṇetabbā. “Chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāvetī”ti vuttaṭṭhānasmiñhi lokuttarāni cattāri nayasahassāni vibhattāni. Vīriyasamādhiādīsupi eseva nayo. Tathā uttaracūḷabhājanīye chandiddhipāde [V 0.0292] cattāri nayasahassāni vibhattāni, vīriyacittavīmaṃsiddhipāde cattāri cattārīti sabbānipi aṭṭhannaṃ catukkānaṃ vasena dvattiṃsa nayasahassāni vibhattāni. Evametaṃ nibbattitalokuttarānaṃyeva iddhipādānaṃ vasena dvattiṃsanayasahassappaṭimaṇḍitaṃ abhidhammabhājanīyaṃ kathitanti veditabbaṃ.

444. The Abhidhamma Exposition is indeed clear in meaning. The methods here, however, should be reckoned. For in the statement, “One develops the basis of psychic power endowed with zeal, concentration, and volitional formations of striving,” four thousand supramundane methods have been classified. The same method applies to energy-concentration and so forth. Similarly, in the subsequent minor exposition, four thousand methods are classified for the zeal-basis of psychic power, and four thousand each for the energy-basis, the mind-basis, and the investigation-basis of psychic power—thus, altogether, thirty-two thousand methods are classified by way of the eight sets of four. Thus, it should be understood that this Abhidhamma Exposition, adorned with thirty-two thousand methods, is taught solely in relation to the supramundane bases of psychic power that have come into being.

3. Pañhāpucchakavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Inquiry Section

462. Pañhāpucchake [M 0.0295] pāḷianusāreneva iddhipādānaṃ kusalādibhāvo veditabbo. Ārammaṇattikesu pana sabbepete appamāṇaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha pavattito appamāṇārammaṇā eva, na maggārammaṇā; sahajātahetuvasena pana maggahetukā, na maggādhipatino. Cattāro hi adhipatayo aññamaññaṃ garuṃ na karonti. Kasmā? Sayaṃ jeṭṭhakattā. Yathā hi samajātikā samavayā samathāmā samasippā cattāro rājaputtā attano attano jeṭṭhakatāya aññamaññassa [P 0.0309] apacitiṃ na karonti, evamimepi cattāro adhipatayo pāṭiyekkaṃ pāṭiyekkaṃ jeṭṭhakadhammatāya aññamaññaṃ garuṃ na karontīti ekanteneva na maggādhipatino. Atītādīsu ekārammaṇabhāvepi na vattabbā. Nibbānassa pana bahiddhādhammattā bahiddhārammaṇā nāma hontīti. Evametasmiṃ pañhāpucchake nibbattitalokuttarāva iddhipādā kathitā. Sammāsambuddhena hi suttantabhājanīyasmiṃyeva lokiyalokuttaramissakā iddhipādā kathitā, abhidhammabhājanīyapañhāpucchakesu pana lokuttarāyevāti. Evamayaṃ iddhipādavibhaṅgopi teparivaṭṭaṃ nīharitvāva dassitoti.

462. In the Inquiry Section, the wholesome and other states of the bases of psychic power should be understood in accordance with the Pāḷi. In the object-triads, however, all these, having arisen with the immeasurable Nibbāna as their object, are indeed of immeasurable object; they are not of path-object. But by way of the co-nascent cause condition, they are path-causes, not path-predominance conditions. For the four predominance conditions do not give weight to one another. Why? Because each is foremost in itself. Just as four princes of equal birth, equal age, equal strength, and equal skill do not show deference to one another due to each considering himself the foremost, so too these four predominance conditions, each being a foremost state in its own right, do not give weight to one another. Therefore, they are definitely not path-predominance conditions. They cannot be said to be so even when sharing a single object in the past, etc. However, since Nibbāna is an external phenomenon, they are called ‘of external object.’ Thus, in this Inquiry Section, only the supramundane bases of psychic power that have come into being are discussed. For the Perfectly Enlightened One taught the bases of psychic power as a mixture of mundane and supramundane only in the Suttanta Exposition, but in the Abhidhamma Exposition and the Inquiry Section, only the supramundane are taught. Thus, this Analysis of the Bases of Psychic Power is also shown only after extracting the three rounds.

Sammohavinodaniyā vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāya

From the Sammohavinodanī, the Commentary to the Vibhaṅga

Iddhipādavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Analysis of the Bases of Psychic Power is concluded.

10. Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgo

10. The Analysis of the Factors of Enlightenment

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. The Explanation of the Suttanta Exposition

466. Idāni [P 0.0310][M 0.0296][V 0.0293] tadanantare bojjhaṅgavibhaṅge sattāti gaṇanaparicchedo. Bojjhaṅgāti bodhiyā bodhissa vā aṅgāti bojjhaṅgā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yā esā dhammasāmaggī yāya lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe uppajjamānāya līnuddhaccapatiṭṭhānāyūhanakāmasukhattakilamathānuyogaucchedasassatābhinivesādīnaṃ anekesaṃ upaddavānaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtāya satidhammavicayavīriyapītipassaddhisamādhiupekkhāsaṅkhātāya dhammasāmaggiyā ariyasāvako bujjhatīti katvā bodhīti vuccati, bujjhati kilesasantānaniddāya uṭṭhahati, cattāri vā ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhati, nibbānameva vā sacchikaroti, tassā dhammasāmaggīsaṅkhātāya bodhiyā aṅgātipi bojjhaṅgā, jhānaṅgamaggaṅgādīni viya. Yo panesa yathāvuttappakārāya etāya dhammasāmaggiyā bujjhatīti katvā ariyasāvako bodhīti vuccati, tassa bodhissa aṅgātipi bojjhaṅgā, senaṅgarathaṅgādayo viya. Tenāhu aṭṭhakathācariyā – “bujjhanakassa puggalassa aṅgāti vā bojjhaṅgā”ti.

466. Now, immediately following that, in the Analysis of the Factors of Enlightenment, “seven” is the numerical determination. “Bojjhaṅgā” means the factors (aṅga) of enlightenment (bodhi) or the factors of the enlightened one (bodhi). This is what is said: There is a certain harmony of dhammas which arises at the moment of the supramundane path. Being an opponent to many troubles such as sloth, restlessness, attachment, exertion, devotion to sensual pleasure and self-mortification, and adherence to annihilationism and eternalism, this harmony of dhammas—designated as mindfulness, investigation-of-dhammas, energy, joy, tranquility, concentration, and equanimity—is called ‘enlightenment’ (bodhi) because the noble disciple awakens (bujjhati) through it. He awakens, that is, he rises from the slumber of the continuity of defilements; or he penetrates the four noble truths; or he directly realizes Nibbāna. The factors of that enlightenment, which is designated as the harmony of dhammas, are also ‘enlightenment factors,’ just like the factors of jhāna or the factors of the path. Furthermore, the noble disciple who awakens through this harmony of dhammas, as described, is called ‘enlightened’ (bodhi), and the factors of that enlightened one are also ‘enlightenment factors,’ like the components of an army or a chariot. Therefore, the commentary teachers have said: “Or, they are the factors of the awakening person.”

Apica “bojjhaṅgāti kenaṭṭhena bojjhaṅgā? Bodhāya saṃvattantīti bojjhaṅgā, bujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, anubujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, paṭibujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā, sambujjhantīti bojjhaṅgā”ti iminā paṭisambhidānayenāpi bojjhaṅgattho veditabbo.

Furthermore, the meaning of ‘enlightenment factors’ should also be understood through the method of the Paṭisambhidāmagga: “‘Enlightenment factors’—in what sense are they enlightenment factors? Because they conduce to enlightenment, they are enlightenment factors; because they awaken, they are enlightenment factors; because they awaken in conformity, they are enlightenment factors; because they awaken to, they are enlightenment factors; because they awaken perfectly, they are enlightenment factors.”

Satisambojjhaṅgotiādīsu pasattho sundaro ca bojjhaṅgo sambojjhaṅgo, satiyeva sambojjhaṅgo satisambojjhaṅgo. Tattha upaṭṭhānalakkhaṇo satisambojjhaṅgo, pavicayalakkhaṇo dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, paggahalakkhaṇo vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pharaṇalakkhaṇo pītisambojjhaṅgo, upasamalakkhaṇo [V 0.0294] passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, avikkhepalakkhaṇo samādhisambojjhaṅgo, paṭisaṅkhānalakkhaṇo [P 0.0311] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Tesu “satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmī”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234) vacanato sabbesaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ upakārakattā satisambojjhaṅgo paṭhamaṃ vutto. Tato paraṃ “so tathā sato viharanto [M 0.0297] taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinatī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 150) nayena evaṃ anukkameneva nikkhepapayojanaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgatameva.

In the terms “mindfulness as a factor of perfect enlightenment” and so forth, a praised and beautiful enlightenment factor is a ‘factor of perfect enlightenment’ (sambojjhaṅga); mindfulness itself is a factor of perfect enlightenment, hence ‘mindfulness as a factor of perfect enlightenment’ (satisambojjhaṅga). Therein, the mindfulness factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of attending; the investigation-of-dhammas factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of investigation; the energy factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of exertion; the joy factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of suffusion; the tranquility factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of calming; the concentration factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of non-distraction; and the equanimity factor of perfect enlightenment has the characteristic of reviewing. Among these, the mindfulness factor of perfect enlightenment is mentioned first because it is helpful to all the factors of perfect enlightenment, as it is said: “Monks, I declare that mindfulness is useful in all circumstances” (SN 48.53). After that, the purpose of the arrangement in this very sequence is just as it comes in the Pāḷi, by the method beginning with: “He, being thus mindful, investigates that dhamma with wisdom…” (MN 118).

Kasmā panete satteva vuttā, anūnā anadhikāti? Līnuddhaccapaṭipakkhato sabbatthikato ca. Ettha hi tayo bojjhaṅgā līnassa paṭipakkhā, yathāha – “yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234). Tayo uddhaccassa paṭipakkhā, yathāha – “yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāyā”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.234). Eko panettha loṇadhūpanaṃ viya sabbabyañjanesu, sabbakammikaamacco viya ca sabbesu rājakiccesu, sabbabojjhaṅgesu icchitabbato sabbatthiko, yathāha – “satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmī”ti. “Sabbatthaka”ntipi pāḷi. Dvinnampi sabbattha icchitabbanti attho. Evaṃ līnuddhaccapaṭipakkhato sabbatthikato ca satteva vuttāti veditabbā.

But why are just these seven mentioned, neither fewer nor more? Because of their opposition to sluggishness and restlessness, and because of being universally applicable. Here, three enlightenment factors counteract sluggishness, as it is said: “Bhikkhus, at the time when the mind is sluggish, that is the time to cultivate the investigation-of-dhamma enlightenment factor, the energy enlightenment factor, and the rapture enlightenment factor” (SN 5.234). Three counteract restlessness, as it is said: “Bhikkhus, at the time when the mind is restless, that is the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, the concentration enlightenment factor, and the equanimity enlightenment factor” (SN 5.234). One here, like salt seasoning all curries, or a minister competent in all the king’s affairs, is desired in all enlightenment factors and is universally applicable, as it is said: “Bhikkhus, I declare that mindfulness is useful in all circumstances.” The Pāli also has the reading “sabbatthaka.” The meaning of both is that it is desired everywhere. Thus, it should be understood that just seven are mentioned because of their opposition to sluggishness and restlessness and because of being universally applicable.

467. Idāni nesaṃ ekasmiṃyevārammaṇe attano attano kiccavasena nānākaraṇaṃ dassetuṃ tattha katamo satisambojjhaṅgotiādi āraddhaṃ. Tattha idha bhikkhūti imasmiṃ sāsane bhikkhu. Satimā hotīti paññāya paññavā, yasena yasavā, dhanena dhanavā viya satiyā satimā hoti, satisampannoti attho. Paramenāti uttamena; tañhi paramatthasaccassa nibbānassa ceva maggassa ca anulomato paramaṃ nāma hoti uttamaṃ seṭṭhaṃ. Satinepakkenāti nepakkaṃ vuccati paññā; satiyā ceva nepakkena [P 0.0312] cāti attho.

467. Now, to show their distinct functions regarding a single object, the following is begun: 'Here, which is the mindfulness enlightenment factor?' and so on. Herein, 'a bhikkhu' means a bhikkhu in this Dispensation. 'Mindful' means that just as one is wise on account of wisdom, famous on account of fame, or wealthy on account of wealth, so one is mindful on account of mindfulness; the meaning is 'endowed with mindfulness.' 'Supreme' means the highest; for it is called supreme, highest, and best because it accords with the ultimate truth of Nibbāna and the path. 'With mindfulness and sagacity' means that sagacity is called wisdom; the meaning is 'with mindfulness and with wisdom.'

Kasmā pana imasmiṃ satibhājanīye paññā saṅgahitāti? Satiyā balavabhāvadīpanatthaṃ. Sati hi paññāya saddhimpi uppajjati vināpi, paññāya saddhiṃ uppajjamānā balavatī hoti, vinā uppajjamānā dubbalā. Tenassā balavabhāvadīpanatthaṃ paññā saṅgahitā. Yathā hi dvīsu [V 0.0295] disāsu dve rājamahāmattā tiṭṭheyyuṃ; tesu eko rājaputtaṃ gahetvā tiṭṭheyya, eko attano dhammatāya ekakova tesu rājaputtaṃ gahetvā ṭhito attanopi [M 0.0298] tejena rājaputtassapi tejena tejavā hoti; attano dhammatāya ṭhito na tena samatejo hoti; evameva rājaputtaṃ gahetvā ṭhitamahāmatto viya paññāya saddhiṃ uppannā sati, attano dhammatāya ṭhito viya vinā paññāya uppannā. Tattha yathā rājaputtaṃ gahetvā ṭhito attanopi tejena rājaputtassapi tejena tejavā hoti, evaṃ paññāya saddhiṃ uppannā sati balavatī hoti; yathā attano dhammatāya ṭhito na tena samatejo hoti, evaṃ vinā paññāya uppannā dubbalā hotīti balavabhāvadīpanatthaṃ paññā gahitāti.

But why, in this exposition on mindfulness, is wisdom included? To demonstrate the power of mindfulness. For mindfulness arises both with and without wisdom; when it arises with wisdom, it is powerful, but when it arises without wisdom, it is weak. Therefore, to demonstrate its power, wisdom is included. Suppose two great royal ministers were standing in two different directions; of these, one stands holding the king’s son, while the other stands alone in his own capacity. The one standing holding the king's son is powerful through his own authority and through the authority of the king's son. The one standing in his own capacity is not equal in authority to him. In the same way, mindfulness arising with wisdom is like the great minister standing holding the king’s son, while mindfulness arising without wisdom is like the one standing in his own capacity. Just as the one standing holding the king's son is powerful through his own authority and through the authority of the king's son, so too is mindfulness arising with wisdom powerful. And just as the one standing in his own capacity is not equal in authority to him, so too is mindfulness arising without wisdom weak. Thus, to demonstrate its power, wisdom is included.

Cirakatampīti attano vā parassa vā kāyena cirakataṃ vattaṃ vā kasiṇamaṇḍalaṃ vā kasiṇaparikammaṃ vā. Cirabhāsitampīti attanā vā parena vā vācāya cirabhāsitaṃ bahukampi, vattasīse ṭhatvā dhammakathaṃ vā kammaṭṭhānavinicchayaṃ vā, vimuttāyatanasīse vā ṭhatvā dhammakathameva. Saritā hotīti taṃ kāyaviññattiṃ vacīviññattiñca samuṭṭhāpetvā pavattaṃ arūpadhammakoṭṭhāsaṃ ‘evaṃ uppajjitvā evaṃ niruddho’ti saritā hoti. Anussaritāti punappunaṃ saritā. Ayaṃ vuccati satisambojjhaṅgoti ayaṃ evaṃ uppannā sesabojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpikā vipassanāsampayuttā sati satisambojjhaṅgo nāma kathīyati.

'Long done' refers to actions long performed by oneself or others with the body: a long-practiced observance, a kasiṇa circle, or kasiṇa preparation. 'Long spoken' refers to many words long spoken by oneself or others: a Dhamma talk or a determination of a meditation subject while standing at the head of an observance, or simply a Dhamma talk while standing at the head of a basis for liberation. 'She remembers' means she remembers the portion of immaterial phenomena that, having been produced by that bodily and verbal intimation, proceeded, thinking, 'Thus it arose, thus it ceased.' 'She recollects' means she remembers again and again. This is called the mindfulness enlightenment factor: this mindfulness, thus arisen, associated with insight, and giving rise to the remaining enlightenment factors, is called the mindfulness enlightenment factor.

So tathā sato viharantoti so bhikkhu tenākārena uppannāya satiyā sato hutvā viharanto. Taṃ dhammanti taṃ cirakataṃ cirabhāsitaṃ heṭṭhā vuttappakāraṃ dhammaṃ. Paññāya pavicinatīti paññāya ‘aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā’ti pavicinati. Pavicaratīti [P 0.0313] ‘aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā’ti tattha paññaṃ carāpento pavicarati. Parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjatīti olokanaṃ gavesanaṃ āpajjati. Ayaṃ vuccatīti idaṃ vuttappakāraṃ bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpakaṃ vipassanāñāṇaṃ dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

He dwells thus mindful: that bhikkhu, dwelling mindful, has become mindful in that way with arisen mindfulness. That Dhamma: that Dhamma, long-practiced and long-spoken, of the kind described above. He discerns with wisdom: he discerns with wisdom as 'impermanent, suffering, not-self.' He investigates: he investigates, applying wisdom to it as 'impermanent, suffering, not-self.' He enters upon examination: he enters upon looking into and searching. This is called: this insight-knowledge of the kind described, which gives rise to the enlightenment factors, is called the enlightenment factor of investigation-of-dhamma.

Tassa taṃ dhammanti tassa bhikkhuno taṃ heṭṭhā vuttappakāraṃ dhammaṃ. Āraddhaṃ hotīti paripuṇṇaṃ hoti paggahitaṃ. Asallīnanti āraddhattāyeva asallīnaṃ. Ayaṃ vuccatīti idaṃ bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpakaṃ vipassanāsampayuttaṃ vīriyaṃ vīriyasambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

For him, that Dhamma: for that bhikkhu, that Dhamma of the kind described above. 'Is aroused' means it is complete, exerted. 'Not slack' means not slack precisely because it is aroused. This is called: this energy, which gives rise to the enlightenment factors and is associated with insight, is called the energy enlightenment factor.

Nirāmisāti [M 0.0299][V 0.0296] kāmāmisalokāmisavaṭṭāmisānaṃ abhāvena nirāmisā parisuddhā. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpikā vipassanāsampayuttā pīti pītisambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

Spiritual: because of the absence of the bait of sensuality, the bait of the world, and the bait of the round of rebirths, it is spiritual and pure. This is called: this rapture, which gives rise to the enlightenment factors and is associated with insight, is called the rapture enlightenment factor.

Pītimanassāti pītisampayuttacittassa. Kāyopi passambhatīti khandhattayasaṅkhāto nāmakāyo kilesadarathapaṭippassaddhiyā passambhati. Cittampīti viññāṇakkhandhopi tatheva passambhati. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpikā vipassanāsampayuttā passaddhi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

One whose mind is joyful means one whose mind is associated with joy. The body also becomes tranquil: the mental body, designated as the three aggregates, becomes tranquil through the calming of the distress of defilements. The mind also—that is, the consciousness aggregate—becomes tranquil in the same way. This is said to be so: this tranquility, which gives rise to the enlightenment factors and is associated with insight, is called the enlightenment factor of tranquility.

Passaddhakāyassa sukhinoti passaddhakāyatāya uppannasukhena sukhitassa. Samādhiyatīti sammā ādhiyati, niccalaṃ hutvā ārammaṇe ṭhapīyati, appanāppattaṃ viya hoti. Ayaṃ vuccatīti ayaṃ bojjhaṅgasamuṭṭhāpikā vipassanāsampayuttā cittekaggatā samādhisambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

One whose body is tranquil is happy: one is happy with the happiness that arises from the tranquility of the body. Becomes concentrated: it is rightly concentrated; being still, it is fixed on the object, as if it has attained absorption. This is said to be so: this one-pointedness of mind, which gives rise to the enlightenment factors and is associated with insight, is called the enlightenment factor of concentration.

Tathā samāhitanti tena appanāppattena viya samādhinā samāhitaṃ. Sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hotīti suṭṭhu ajjhupekkhitā hoti; tesaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānavaḍḍhane abyāvaṭo hutvā ajjhupekkhati. Ayaṃ [P 0.0314] vuccatīti ayaṃ channaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ anosakkanaanativattanabhāvasādhako majjhattākāro upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nāma vuccati.

Thus composed: one is composed by that concentration, as if attained to absorption. Perfectly looks on with equanimity: one looks on well with equanimity, being undisturbed and not preoccupied with the abandoning and growth of those states. This is said to be so: this neutral aspect, which accomplishes the state of not shrinking back from or overstepping the six enlightenment factors, is called the enlightenment factor of equanimity.

Ettāvatā kiṃ kathitaṃ nāma hoti? Apubbaṃ acarimaṃ ekacittakkhaṇe nānārasalakkhaṇā pubbabhāgavipassanā bojjhaṅgā kathitā hontīti.

By this much, what is said to have been explained? The enlightenment factors, which are preliminary insight, arising neither before nor after one another, with diverse characteristics and functions in a single mind-moment, have been explained.

Paṭhamo nayo.

The first method.

468-469. Idāni yena pariyāyena satta bojjhaṅgā cuddasa honti, tassa pakāsanatthaṃ dutiyanayaṃ dassento puna satta bojjhaṅgātiādimāha. Tatrāyaṃ anupubbapadavaṇṇanā – ajjhattaṃ dhammesu satīti ajjhattikasaṅkhāre pariggaṇhantassa uppannā sati. Bahiddhā dhammesu satīti bahiddhāsaṅkhāre pariggaṇhantassa uppannā sati. Yadapīti yāpi. Tadapīti sāpi. Abhiññāyāti abhiññeyyadhamme abhijānanatthāya. Sambodhāyāti sambodhi vuccati maggo, maggatthāyāti attho. Nibbānāyāti [V 0.0297] vānaṃ vuccati taṇhā; sā tattha [M 0.0300] natthīti nibbānaṃ, tadatthāya, asaṅkhatāya amatadhātuyā sacchikiriyatthāya saṃvattatīti attho. Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgepi eseva nayo.

Now, to explain the way in which the seven enlightenment factors become fourteen, showing the second method, he said again, 'the seven enlightenment factors,' and so on. Here is the sequential explanation of the terms: 'Internally, mindfulness of phenomena' refers to mindfulness that arises when one comprehends internal formations. 'Externally, mindfulness of phenomena' refers to mindfulness that arises when one comprehends external formations. 'Whatever' means 'which also.' 'That too' means 'that also.' 'For direct knowledge' means for the purpose of directly knowing the knowable phenomena. 'For awakening' means the path is called awakening; it is for the sake of the path. 'For Nibbāna' means craving is called 'vāna'; because it is absent there, it is Nibbāna. It is for the sake of that, for the realization of the unconditioned, deathless element. The same method applies to the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.

Kāyikaṃ vīriyanti caṅkamaṃ adhiṭṭhahantassa uppannavīriyaṃ. Cetasikaṃ vīriyanti “na tāvāhaṃ imaṃ pallaṅkaṃ bhindissāmi yāva me na anupādāya āsavehi cittaṃ vimuccissatī”ti evaṃ kāyapayogaṃ vinā uppannavīriyaṃ. Kāyapassaddhīti tiṇṇaṃ khandhānaṃ darathapassaddhi. Cittapassaddhīti viññāṇakkhandhassa darathapassaddhi. Upekkhāsambojjhaṅge satisambojjhaṅgasadisova vinicchayo. Imasmiṃ naye satta bojjhaṅgā lokiyalokuttaramissakā kathitā.

Bodily energy is the energy that arises for one who undertakes walking meditation. Mental energy is the energy that arises without bodily exertion, with the resolve: 'I will not break this cross-legged posture until my mind is liberated from the taints without clinging.' Bodily tranquility is the calming of distress of the three aggregates. Mental tranquility is the calming of distress of the consciousness aggregate. With regard to the enlightenment factor of equanimity, the explanation is similar to that of the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. In this method, the seven enlightenment factors are described as a mixture of the mundane and the supramundane.

Porāṇakattherā pana ‘ettakena pākaṭaṃ na hotī’ti vibhajitvā dassesuṃ. Etesu hi ajjhattadhammesu sati pavicayo upekkhāti ime tayo attano khandhārammaṇattā lokiyāva honti. Tathā maggaṃ appattaṃ kāyikavīriyaṃ. Avitakkaavicārā [P 0.0315] pana pītisamādhiyo lokuttarā honti. Sesā lokiyalokuttaramissakāti.

The ancient elders, however, explained by analyzing, saying, 'By this much, it is not made clear.' Among these, these three regarding internal phenomena—mindfulness, investigation of phenomena, and equanimity—because their object is one's own aggregates, are purely mundane. Similarly, bodily energy that has not yet attained the path is mundane. But the joy and concentration free from thought and examination are supramundane. The rest are a mixture of the mundane and the supramundane.

Tattha ajjhattaṃ tāva dhammesu satipavicayaupekkhā ajjhattārammaṇā, lokuttarā pana bahiddhārammaṇāti tesaṃ lokuttarabhāvo mā yujjittha. Caṅkamappayogena nibbattavīriyampi lokiyanti vadanto na kilamati. Avitakkaavicārā pana pītisamādhiyo kadā lokuttarā hontīti? Kāmāvacare tāva pītisambojjhaṅgo labbhati, avitakkaavicārā pīti na labbhati. Rūpāvacare avitakkaavicārā pīti labbhati, pītisambojjhaṅgo pana na labbhati. Arūpāvacare sabbena sabbaṃ na labbhati. Ettha pana alabbhamānakaṃ upādāya labbhamānakāpi paṭikkhittā. Evamayaṃ avitakkaavicāro pītisambojjhaṅgo kāmāvacaratopi nikkhanto rūpāvacaratopi arūpāvacaratopīti nibbattitalokuttaro yevāti kathito.

Herein, firstly, mindfulness, investigation of phenomena, and equanimity regarding internal phenomena have an internal object, but the supramundane has an external object—lest their supramundane nature be inappropriately connected. One who asserts that even the energy produced by the practice of walking meditation is mundane does not falter. But when do joy and concentration free from thought and examination become supramundane? Firstly, in the sense sphere, the enlightenment factor of joy is obtained, but joy free from thought and examination is not obtained. In the form sphere, joy free from thought and examination is obtained, but the enlightenment factor of joy is not obtained. In the formless sphere, absolutely nothing is obtained. Here, however, by taking what is unobtainable as a basis, even what is obtainable is rejected. Thus, this enlightenment factor of joy, free from thought and examination, having emerged from the sense sphere, the form sphere, and the formless sphere, is declared to be exclusively supramundane.

Tathā kāmāvacare samādhisambojjhaṅgo labbhati, avitakkaavicāro pana samādhi na labbhati. Rūpāvacaraarūpāvacaresu avitakkaavicāro samādhi labbhati, samādhisambojjhaṅgo pana na labbhati. Ettha pana alabbhamānakaṃ upādāya labbhamānakopi paṭikkhitto. Evamayaṃ avitakkaavicāro samādhi kāmāvacaratopi nikkhanto rūpāvacaratopi arūpāvacaratopīti nibbattitalokuttaro yevāti kathito.

Similarly, the enlightenment factor of concentration is obtained in the sense sphere, but concentration free from thought and examination is not obtained. In the form sphere and formless sphere, concentration free from thought and examination is obtained, but the enlightenment factor of concentration is not obtained. Here, however, by taking what is unobtainable as a basis, even what is obtainable is rejected. Thus, this concentration free from thought and examination, having emerged from the sense sphere, the form sphere, and the formless sphere, is declared to be exclusively supramundane.

Apica [M 0.0301][V 0.0298] lokiyaṃ gahetvā lokuttaro kātabbo; lokuttaraṃ gahetvā lokiyo kātabbo. Ajjhattadhammesu hi satipavicayaupekkhānaṃ lokuttarabhāvanākālopi atthi. Tatridaṃ suttaṃ – “ajjhattavimokkhaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sabbupādānakkhayaṃ vadāmi; evamassime āsavā nānusentī”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.32 thokaṃ visadisaṃ) iminā suttena lokuttarā honti. Yadā pana caṅkamapayogena nibbatte kāyikavīriye anupasanteyeva vipassanā maggena ghaṭīyati, tadā taṃ lokuttaraṃ hoti. Ye pana therā “kasiṇajjhāne, ānāpānajjhāne, brahmavihārajjhāne ca bojjhaṅgo uddharanto na vāretabbo”ti vadanti, tesaṃ vāde avitakkaavicārā pītisamādhisambojjhaṅgā lokiyā hontīti.

Moreover, having taken the mundane, one should make it supramundane; having taken the supramundane, one should make it mundane. For in internal phenomena there is even a time for the supramundane development of mindfulness, investigation of states, and equanimity. Here is the sutta: 'Friend, I declare internal liberation to be the destruction of all grasping; thus, these taints do not lie latent in him.' By this sutta, they are supramundane. But when, by means of the application of walking meditation, bodily energy arises and, without it being calmed, one strives with the path of insight, then that is supramundane. However, according to the view of those elders who say, 'One should not be prevented from arousing an enlightenment factor in kasiṇa-jhāna, ānāpāna-jhāna, and brahmavihāra-jhāna,' the enlightenment factors of joy and concentration, which are without initial and sustained thought, are mundane.

Dutiyo nayo.

The second method.

470-471. Idāni [P 0.0316] bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvanāvasena pavattaṃ tatiyanayaṃ dassento puna satta bojjhaṅgātiādimāha. Tatthāpi ayaṃ anupubbapadavaṇṇanā – bhāvetīti vaḍḍheti; attano santāne punappunaṃ janeti abhinibbatteti. Vivekanissitanti viveke nissitaṃ. Vivekoti vivittatā. So cāyaṃ tadaṅgaviveko, vikkhambhanasamucchedapaṭippassaddhinissaraṇavivekoti pañcavidho. Tattha tadaṅgaviveko nāma vipassanā. Vikkhambhanaviveko nāma aṭṭha samāpattiyo. Samucchedaviveko nāma maggo. Paṭippassaddhiviveko nāma phalaṃ. Nissaraṇaviveko nāma sabbanimittanissaṭaṃ nibbānaṃ. Evametasmiṃ pañcavidhe viveke nissitaṃ vivekanissitanti tadaṅgavivekanissitaṃ samucchedavivekanissitaṃ nissaraṇavivekanissitañca satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvetīti ayamattho veditabbo.

470-471. Now, to show the third method that proceeds by way of developing the enlightenment factors, he says again, beginning with 'seven enlightenment factors.' Herein, this is the word-by-word explanation in sequence: 'Develops' means increases; repeatedly generates and brings into being in one's own continuity. 'Dependent on seclusion' means dependent on seclusion. 'Seclusion' means separateness. And this seclusion is fivefold: seclusion by substitution of opposites, seclusion by suppression, seclusion by eradication, seclusion by tranquilization, and seclusion by escape. Herein, 'seclusion by substitution of opposites' is insight. 'Seclusion by suppression' is the eight attainments. 'Seclusion by eradication' is the path. 'Seclusion by tranquilization' is the fruit. 'Seclusion by escape' is Nibbāna, which has escaped from all signs. Thus, 'dependent on seclusion' (vivekanissitaṃ) means dependent on this fivefold seclusion; it should be understood that this means one develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor as dependent on seclusion by substitution of opposites, dependent on seclusion by eradication, and dependent on seclusion by escape.

Tathā hi ayaṃ satisambojjhaṅgabhāvanānuyogamanuyutto yogī vipassanākkhaṇe kiccato tadaṅgavivekanissitaṃ, ajjhāsayato nissaraṇavivekanissitaṃ, maggakāle pana kiccato samucchedavivekanissitaṃ, ārammaṇato nissaraṇavivekanissitaṃ, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti. Pañcavivekanissitampīti eke. Te hi na kevalaṃ balavavipassanāmaggaphalakkhaṇesu eva bojjhaṅgaṃ uddharanti, vipassanāpādakakasiṇajjhānaānāpānāsubhabrahmavihārajjhānesupi uddharanti, na ca paṭisiddhā aṭṭhakathācariyehi[M 0.0302]. Tasmā tesaṃ matena etesaṃ jhānānaṃ pavattikkhaṇe kiccato eva vikkhambhanavivekanissitaṃ. Yathā ca vipassanākkhaṇe “ajjhāsayato nissaraṇavivekanissita”nti [V 0.0299] vuttaṃ, evaṃ “paṭippassaddhivivekanissitampi bhāvetī”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Esa nayo virāganissitādīsu. Vivekatthā eva hi virāgādayo.

For this yogi, devoted to the practice of developing the mindfulness enlightenment factor, develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor as dependent on seclusion by substitution of opposites in terms of function at the moment of insight, and as dependent on seclusion by escape in terms of inclination; and at the time of the path, as dependent on seclusion by eradication in terms of function and as dependent on seclusion by escape in terms of object. Some say it is also dependent on the five seclusions. For they arouse the enlightenment factor not only during the moments of strong insight, path, and fruition, but also in the jhānas that are the basis for insight—kasiṇa-jhāna, ānāpāna-jhāna, meditation on foulness, and the brahmavihāra-jhānas—and they are not refuted by the commentary masters. Therefore, according to their view, at the moment these jhānas arise, it is dependent on seclusion by suppression in terms of function. And just as it is said, 'dependent on seclusion by escape in terms of inclination' at the moment of insight, so too it is fitting to say, 'one also develops it as dependent on seclusion by tranquilization.' This method applies to being dependent on dispassion, etc., for dispassion and so on have the meaning of seclusion.

Kevalañcettha vossaggo duvidho – pariccāgavossaggo ca pakkhandanavossaggo cāti. Tattha ‘pariccāgavossaggo’ti vipassanākkhaṇe ca tadaṅgavasena maggakkhaṇe ca samucchedavasena kilesappahānaṃ. ‘Pakkhandanavossaggo’ti vipassanākkhaṇe tanninnabhāvena, maggakkhaṇe pana ārammaṇakaraṇena nibbānapakkhandanaṃ. Tadubhayampi imasmiṃ lokiyalokuttaramissake [P 0.0317] atthavaṇṇanānaye vaṭṭati. Tathā hi ayaṃ sati sambojjhaṅgo yathāvuttena pakārena kilese pariccajati, nibbānañca pakkhandati.

Here, relinquishment is twofold: the relinquishment of abandonment and the relinquishment of plunging. In this context, 'the relinquishment of abandonment' refers to the abandoning of defilements by way of substitution of opposites during the moment of insight, and by way of eradication during the moment of the path. 'The relinquishment of plunging' refers to the plunging toward Nibbāna by inclining towards it during the moment of insight, and by making it the object during the moment of the path. Both of these apply in this mixed explanation of mundane and supramundane meaning. For this mindfulness enlightenment factor, in the manner described, abandons defilements and plunges toward Nibbāna.

Vossaggapariṇāminti iminā pana sakalena vacanena vossaggatthaṃ pariṇamantaṃ pariṇatañca, paripaccantaṃ paripakkañcāti idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti. Ayañhi bojjhaṅgabhāvanamanuyutto bhikkhu yathā satisambojjhaṅgo kilesapariccāgavossaggatthaṃ nibbānapakkhandanavossaggatthañca paripaccati, yathā ca paripakko hoti, tathā naṃ bhāvetīti. Esa nayo sesabojjhaṅgesupi. Imasmimpi naye lokiyalokuttaramissakā bojjhaṅgā kathitāti.

By this entire statement, 'culminating in relinquishment' (vossaggapariṇāmi), it is said that it is inclining toward the purpose of relinquishment and has so inclined; it is maturing and has become fully mature. For a monk devoted to the cultivation of the enlightenment factors cultivates the mindfulness enlightenment factor in such a way that it matures for the purpose of the relinquishment of abandoning defilements and the relinquishment of plunging into Nibbāna, and in such a way that it becomes fully mature. This is the method for the remaining enlightenment factors as well. In this method, the enlightenment factors are discussed as a mixture of the mundane and supramundane.

Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā.

The Commentary on the Suttanta Exposition.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. The Commentary on the Abhidhamma Exposition.

472. Abhidhammabhājanīye sattapi bojjhaṅge ekato pucchitvā vissajjanassa ca pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanassa ca vasena dve nayā. Tesaṃ atthavaṇṇanā heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbā.

472. In the Abhidhamma Exposition, there are two methods: one by way of questioning and answering about all seven enlightenment factors together, and one by way of questioning and answering about each individually. The explanation of their meaning should be understood in the same manner as stated above.

Upekkhāsambojjhaṅganiddese pana upekkhanavasena upekkhā. Upekkhanākāro upekkhanā. Upekkhitabbayutte samappavatte dhamme ikkhati, na codetīti [M 0.0303] upekkhā. Puggalaṃ upekkhāpetīti upekkhanā[V 0.0300]. Bojjhaṅgabhāvappattiyā lokiyaupekkhanāya adhikā upekkhanā ajjhupekkhanā. Abyāpārāpajjanena majjhattabhāvo majjhattatā. Sā pana cittassa, na sattassāti dīpetuṃ majjhattatā cittassāti vuttanti. Ayamettha anupubbapadavaṇṇanā.

In the exposition of the equanimity enlightenment factor, equanimity (upekkhā) is so called because of its nature of looking on (upekkhanā). The mode of looking on is equanimity. It observes phenomena that should be regarded with equanimity as they proceed evenly, without interfering—thus it is equanimity (upekkhā). It causes a person to look on with equanimity—thus it is 'looking on' (upekkhana). Because it has attained the state of an enlightenment factor, it is a higher equanimity, exceeding worldly equanimity—it is thorough equanimity (ajjhupekkhanā). Impartiality (majjhattatā) is the state of being neutral, through not becoming engaged. But to show that this impartiality belongs to the mind, not to a being, it is said, 'impartiality of the mind.' This here is the sequential word-by-word explanation.

Nayā panettha gaṇetabbā – sattannampi hi bojjhaṅgānaṃ ekato pucchitvā vissajjane ekekamagge nayasahassaṃ nayasahassanti cattāri nayasahassāni vibhattāni. Pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchitvā vissajjane ekekabojjhaṅgavasena cattāri cattārīti satta catukkā aṭṭhavīsati. Tāni purimehi catūhi saddhiṃ dvattiṃsāti sabbānipi abhidhammabhājanīye dvattiṃsa nayasahassāni vibhattāni kusalāneva. Yasmā pana phalakkhaṇepi bojjhaṅgā labbhanti, kusalahetukāni ca sāmaññaphalāni, tasmā tesupi bojjhaṅgadassanatthaṃ kusalaniddesapubbaṅgamāya eva tantiyā vipākanayo āraddho. Sopi [P 0.0318] ekato pucchitvā vissajjanassa ca, pāṭiyekkaṃ pucchitvā vissajjanassa ca vasena duvidho hoti. Sesamettha heṭṭhā vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Vipāke pana kusalato tiguṇā nayā kātabbāti.

Here, the modes should be reckoned thus: when all seven enlightenment factors are asked about and explained together, for each path there are a thousand modes, so four thousand modes are distinguished. When each is asked about and explained separately, by way of each enlightenment factor there are four thousand modes each, thus seven sets of four thousand are twenty-eight thousand. These, together with the previous four thousand, total thirty-two thousand; thus in the Abhidhamma Exposition, all thirty-two thousand modes are distinguished only in regard to the wholesome. Since the enlightenment factors are also found in the fruition moment, and the fruits of recluseship are rooted in the wholesome, therefore, to show the enlightenment factors in them too, the method of the resultant is begun with the wholesome classification as a preamble. That too is twofold, based on asking and explaining all together, and asking and explaining each separately. The remainder here should be understood in the same way as explained previously. But regarding the resultant, the modes should be made three times those of the wholesome.

Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā.

Commentary on the Abhidhamma Exposition.

3. Pañhāpucchakavaṇṇanā

3. Commentary on the Section of Questions

482. Pañhāpucchake pāḷianusāreneva bojjhaṅgānaṃ kusalādibhāvo veditabbo. Ārammaṇattikesu pana sabbepete appamāṇaṃ nibbānaṃ ārabbha pavattito appamāṇārammaṇā eva, na maggārammaṇā. Sahajātahetuvasena panettha kusalā maggahetukā, vīriyaṃ vā vīmaṃsaṃ vā jeṭṭhakaṃ katvā maggabhāvanākāle maggādhipatino, chandacittajeṭṭhikāya maggabhāvanāya na vattabbā maggādhipatinoti, phalakālepi na vattabbā eva.

482. In the Section of Questions, the wholesome and other natures of the enlightenment factors should be understood according to the Pāli text. However, among the triads concerning objects, all these are states with an immeasurable object, having arisen with reference to the immeasurable Nibbāna, not states with the path as object. But here, in terms of co-nascent condition, the wholesome factors are path-caused. When energy or investigation is made pre-eminent at the time of developing the path, they are path-dominant. However, when the path is developed with desire or consciousness as pre-eminent, they should not be called path-dominant; nor should they be called so at the fruition moment.

Atītādīsu ekārammaṇabhāvenapi na vattabbā, nibbānassa pana bahiddhādhammattā bahiddhārammaṇā nāma hontīti. Evametasmiṃ pañhāpucchakepi nibbattitalokuttarāva [M 0.0304] bojjhaṅgā kathitā[V 0.0301]. Sammāsambuddhena hi suttantabhājanīyasseva paṭhamanayasmiṃ lokiyā, dutiyatatiyesu lokiyalokuttaramissakā bojjhaṅgā kathitā. Abhidhammabhājanīyassa pana catūsupi nayesu imasmiñca pañhāpucchake lokuttarāyevāti evamayaṃ bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgopi teparivaṭṭaṃ nīharitvāva bhājetvā dassitoti.

In the past and so forth, they cannot be spoken of as having a single object, but since Nibbāna is an external phenomenon, they are called 'having an external object.' Thus, even in this Section of Questions, only the supramundane enlightenment factors that have arisen are taught. For by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, in the first method of the Suttanta Classification, only the mundane enlightenment factors were taught; in the second and third, mixed mundane and supramundane enlightenment factors were taught. But in the Abhidhamma Classification, in all four methods and in this Section of Questions as well, only the supramundane are taught. Thus, this Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors is shown after extracting and dividing it into these three rounds.

Sammohavinodaniyā vibhaṅgaṭṭhakathāya

In the Sammohavinodanī, the Commentary on the Vibhaṅga.

Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅgavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors is concluded.

11. Maggaṅgavibhaṅgo

11. The Analysis of the Path Factors

1. Suttantabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Suttanta Classification

486. Idāni [P 0.0319][M 0.0305][V 0.0302] tadanantare maggavibhaṅge ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggotiādi sabbaṃ saccavibhaṅge dukkhanirodhagāminīpaṭipadāniddese vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Bhāvanāvasena pāṭiyekkaṃ dassite dutiyanayepi sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitantiādi sabbaṃ bojjhaṅgavibhaṅge vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Evamidaṃ dvinnampi nayānaṃ vasena suttantabhājanīyaṃ lokiyalokuttaramissakameva kathitaṃ.

486. Now, immediately following that, in the Analysis of the Path, the passage beginning 'the noble eight-factored path' and so forth—all should be understood in the manner explained in the Analysis of the Truths, in the exposition of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. In the second method, where it is shown separately by way of development, the passage beginning 'one develops right view based on seclusion' and so forth—all should be understood in the manner explained in the Analysis of the Enlightenment Factors. Thus, this Suttanta Classification has been taught as a mixture of both mundane and supramundane, according to these two methods.

2. Abhidhammabhājanīyavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Abhidhamma Classification

490. Abhidhammabhājanīye ‘ariyo’ti avatvā aṭṭhaṅgiko maggoti vuttaṃ. Evaṃ avuttepi ayaṃ ariyo eva. Yathā hi muddhābhisittassa rañño muddhābhisittāya deviyā kucchismiṃ jāto putto rājaputtoti avuttepi rājaputtoyeva hoti, evamayampi ariyoti avuttepi ariyo evāti veditabbo. Sesamidhāpi saccavibhaṅge vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

490. In the Abhidhamma Classification, instead of saying 'noble,' it says 'the eight-factored path.' Even though it is not stated thus, this is indeed noble. Just as a son born from the womb of a king's consecrated queen, even if not called a prince, is still a prince, so too, even if this is not called 'noble,' it should be understood as noble. The rest here should also be understood in the same way as explained in the Analysis of the Truths.

493. Pañcaṅgikavārepi aṭṭhaṅgikoti avuttepi aṭṭhaṅgiko eva veditabbo. Lokuttaramaggo hi pañcaṅgiko nāma natthi. Ayamettha ācariyānaṃ samānatthakathā. Vitaṇḍavādī panāha – “lokuttaramaggo aṭṭhaṅgiko nāma natthi, pañcaṅgikoyeva hotī”ti. So “suttaṃ āharāhī”ti vutto addhā aññaṃ apassanto imaṃ mahāsaḷāyatanato suttappadesaṃ āharissati “yā tathābhūtassa diṭṭhi, sāssa hoti sammādiṭṭhi. Yo tathābhūtassa saṅkappo, vāyāmo, sati, yo [V 0.0303] tathābhūtassa samādhi, svāssa hoti sammāsamādhi. Pubbeva kho panassa kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ ājīvo suparisuddho hotī”ti.

493. Even in the section on the five-factored path, though it is not stated as eight-factored, it should still be understood as eight-factored. For there is no such thing as a five-factored supramundane path. This is the common explanation of the teachers here. However, a sophist says: "There is no such thing as an eight-factored supramundane path; it is only five-factored." When told, "Bring forth a sutta," and finding no other, he will certainly cite this passage from the Mahāsaḷāyatana Sutta: "Whatever is the view of one who is such, that is his right view. Whatever is the thought, the effort, the mindfulness, whatever is the concentration of one who is such, that is his right concentration. Moreover, his bodily action, verbal action, and livelihood are already well-purified."

Tato “etassa anantaraṃ suttapadaṃ āharā”ti vattabbo. Sace āharati iccetaṃ kusalaṃ, no ce āharati sayaṃ āharitvā “evamassāyaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti (ma. ni. 3.431) “iminā [P 0.0320][M 0.0306] te satthusāsanena vādo bhinno; lokuttaramaggo pañcaṅgiko nāma natthi, aṭṭhaṅgikova hotī”ti vattabbo.

Then, he should be told: "Bring forth the next passage of the sutta." If he brings it forth, that is good. If he does not bring it forth, one should bring it forth oneself and say: "'Thus this Noble Eight-factored Path goes to the fulfillment of development' (MN 149). By this teaching of the Teacher, your argument is refuted; there is no five-factored supramundane path, it is only eight-factored."

Imāni pana tīṇi aṅgāni pubbe parisuddhāni vattanti, lokuttaramaggakkhaṇe parisuddhatarāni honti. Atha ‘pañcaṅgiko maggo’ti idaṃ kimatthaṃ gahitanti? Atirekakiccadassanatthaṃ. Yasmiñhi samaye micchāvācaṃ pajahati, sammāvācaṃ pūreti, tasmiṃ samaye sammākammantasammāājīvā natthi. Imāni pañcakārāpakaṅgāneva micchāvācaṃ pajahanti; sammāvācā pana sayaṃ virativasena pūreti. Yasmiṃ samaye micchākammantaṃ pajahati, sammākammantaṃ pūreti, tasmiṃ samaye sammāvācāsammāājīvā natthi. Imāni pañca kārāpakaṅgāneva micchākammantaṃ pajahanti; sammākammanto pana sayaṃ virativasena pūreti. Yasmiṃ samaye micchāājīvaṃ pajahati, sammāājīvaṃ pūreti, tasmiṃ samaye sammāvācāsammākammantā natthi. Imāni pañca kārāpakaṅgāneva micchāājīvaṃ pajahanti; sammāājīvo pana sayaṃ virativasena pūreti. Imaṃ etesaṃ pañcannaṃ kārāpakaṅgānaṃ kiccātirekataṃ dassetuṃ pañcaṅgiko maggoti gahitaṃ. Lokuttaramaggo pana aṭṭhaṅgikova hoti, pañcaṅgiko nāma natthi.

Moreover, these three factors exist in a purified state beforehand, but at the moment of the supramundane path, they become even more purified. Then, why is the term 'five-factored path' used? To show the exceeding of function. For when one abandons wrong speech and fulfills right speech, at that time, right action and right livelihood are not present. These five causative factors alone abandon wrong speech; but right speech fulfills itself by way of abstinence. When one abandons wrong action and fulfills right action, at that time, right speech and right livelihood are not present. These five causative factors alone abandon wrong action; but right action fulfills itself by way of abstinence. When one abandons wrong livelihood and fulfills right livelihood, at that time, right speech and right action are not present. These five causative factors alone abandon wrong livelihood; but right livelihood fulfills itself by way of abstinence. The term 'five-factored path' is used to illustrate this exceeding of function of these five causative factors. However, the supramundane path is only eight-factored; there is no such thing as a five-factored path.

“Yadi sammāvācādīhi saddhiṃ aṭṭhaṅgikoti vadatha, catasso sammāvācācetanā, tisso sammākammantacetanā, satta sammāājīvacetanāti imamhā cetanābahuttā kathaṃ muccissatha?
